The purpose of this position paper is to formally document the basis behind the design decision to incorporate all the functions associated with the Radioactive Waste Building (RWB) into the Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB) for the SMR-300 project at the Covert, Michigan Palisades site as well as all other future locations.

This design decision process was started shortly after the RWB required equipment, layout, and scope, were initially determined. The design decision process itself was carried out in phases that involved all the applicable stakeholders and key decision makers (detailed within). After weighing out many considerations based on reasonable assumptions, estimates, and the best available data at the time, the decision was made to incorporate the RWB functions into the RAB and remove the RWB from the Plot Plan.

entries.text: Operational Experience from existing nuclear power stations that currently have liquid radioactive waste processing in the same equivalent building as the RAB is assumed to be relevant even though the SMR-300 systems are not yet designed.

Table 2-1 lists the relevant requirements found in the SMR-300 Top Level Plant Design Requirements [4], a combination of both updated SMR-160 Objectives as well the relevant EPRI URD [3] requirements, that must be considered whether the waste processing facility is separate or absorbed by another structure.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The plant arrangement and building design features shall be defined to enhance the plant's capabilities to resist external threats of radiological sabotage.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The plant shall provide systems to store and manage the handling of liquid, gaseous, and solid radioactive waste and provide any necessary temporary storage. The best available technology shall be adopted. Storage capacity shall be at least: Liquid Radioactive Waste Capacity: 14 days or greater Solid Radioactive Waste Capacity: 30 days or greater

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The plant design shall include facilities and equipment to transfer spent fuel from wet storage to hardened (e.g. resistant to external conditions such as weather or missiles) dry storage casks located onsite and include adequate margin for temporary increases in the generation of such waste.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The capability to store six months or more production of low-level waste shall be provided.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The design shall provide adequate access space for maintenance, testing, operation, and component removal or replacement necessary to achieve plant design life.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The plant arrangement and the design of buildings shall provide for the control of personnel and movement of materials with a minimum of security and radiological control points to minimize security force requirements.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: Modularity concepts shall be applied to the design of systems and structures that are economical. The evaluation of economics shall consider the net impact on construction, including schedule, cost, and transportation logistics.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The design and layout of SSCs shall maximize the efficiency of serial construction of multiple units by preferring the specification of identical arrangements, sizes, and orientations in the design of areas, systems, equipment, components, and bulk commodities. The use of mirroring shall be avoided to the extent practical.

entries.section_title: Several Action Items were identified for follow-up at the conclusion of the meeting:
entries.text: 1) Confirm with Hyundai Engineering and Construction (HDEC) the RWB itself, being utilized as a terminal point and collector area for electrical and mechanical utilities (e.g. gas systems, demineralized water, etc.), may be eliminated with minimal impact and/or considerations. HDEC confirmed the elimination of this building will not affect the distribution of electrical and mechanical utilities adversely.

entries.section_title: Several Action Items were identified for follow-up at the conclusion of the meeting:
entries.text: Outcome: HDEC confirmed the elimination of this building will not affect the distribution of electrical and mechanical utilities adversely.

entries.section_title: Several Action Items were identified for follow-up at the conclusion of the meeting:
entries.text: Status: This action item is considered closed.

entries.section_title: Several Action Items were identified for follow-up at the conclusion of the meeting:
entries.text: 2) Confirm what additional impact on the LWA, if any, will be, if any.

entries.section_title: Several Action Items were identified for follow-up at the conclusion of the meeting:
entries.text: Outcome: The actual impact on the LWA will not be determined for many months until the actual submittal. Nonetheless, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) has already been sent an outline letter that identifies the rad waste systems, structures, and components as non-construction (meaning, not in the scope of construction as defined by 10 CFR 50.10, License Required; Limited Work Authorization). As such, this construction scope could be performed ahead of the construction permit issuance. However, even though the specifics around this approach may change, the RWB absorption into the RAB should have no impact on this. Therefore, this will not adversely affect the LWA submittal or review.

entries.section_title: Several Action Items were identified for follow-up at the conclusion of the meeting:
entries.text: Status: This action item is considered closed.

entries.section_title: Several Action Items were identified for follow-up at the conclusion of the meeting:
entries.text: 3) Confirm seismic interactions are simplified based on the elimination of the RWB and the consolidation of the RAB base mat [9].

entries.section_title: Several Action Items were identified for follow-up at the conclusion of the meeting:
entries.text: Outcome: The civil/structural team confirmed a single base mat for the RAB, verses a stepped base mat, combined with a single mat for an entire building, will result in a simplified Soil Structure Interaction (SSI) analysis model, improved seismic response and elimination of seismic isolation joints between Radiological Controlled Area (RCA) and Main Control Room (MCR) area within the Control Building (CB) portion of the RAB, and RAB and RWB themselves.

entries.text: The purpose of this position paper is to formally document the basis behind the design decision to incorporate all the functions associated with the Radioactive Waste Building (RWB) into the Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB) for the SMR-300 project at the Covert, Michigan Palisades site as well as all other future locations. This design decision process was started shortly after the RWB required equipment, layout, and scope, were initially determined. The design decision process itself was carried out in phases that involved all the applicable stakeholders and key decision makers (detailed within). After weighing out many considerations based on reasonable assumptions, estimates, and the best available data at the time, the decision was made to incorporate the RWB functions into the RAB and remove the RWB from the Plot Plan.
To document the rationale and decision-making process behind incorporating the Radioactive Waste Building (RWB) functions into the Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB).

The decision to incorporate the RWB functions into the RAB was initiated after the initial determination of the RWB's required equipment, layout, and scope. The process involved multiple stakeholders and decision-makers.
The decision was based on reasonable assumptions, estimates, and the best available data at the time.

The purpose of this report is to formally document the decision and basis behind evaluating keeping a separate Radioactive Waste Building (RWB or incorporation of all the functions associated with a separate RWB into the Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB) for the SMR-300 project at the Covert, Michigan (Palisades). This Palisades SMR-300 site will serve as a reference project and may serve as a reference design for other future locations.

This design decision is a Category 2 decision in accordance with HPP-8002-0003 [6] because it has been preliminarily determined to affect several engineering disciplines, including configuration of applicable systems and pipe routing in addition to the building design specifications.

The conclusion of this decision paper will inform changes required to the design documentation of the RWB and RAB. As an example, the RAB Drawings [9] are expected to be revised and RWB Drawing [11] obsoleted.

This Palisades SMR-300 site will serve as a reference project and may serve as a reference design for other future locations.

This design decision is a Category 2 decision in accordance with HPP-8002-0003 [6] because it has been preliminarily determined to affect several engineering disciplines, including configuration of applicable systems and pipe routing in addition to the building design specifications.

The conclusion of this decision paper will inform changes required to the design documentation of the RWB and RAB. As an example, the RAB Drawings [9] are expected to be revised and RWB Drawing [11] obsoleted.

The draft layout of the RWB [11] was issued by the Civil Structural team once the functional requirements as determined and specified by a Holtec subcontractor, Enercon. Upon reviewal of the building requirements, layout, and functions to be housed, a potential optimization opportunity was identified where the functions of the building could potentially be placed inside the RAB [9] through the expansion of the existing -38' Elevation underneath the non-radiological portion of the Control Building.

A small team of critical stakeholders (Operations, Civil/Structural, and Capital Expenditure) evaluated the RWB structure and functions in accordance with Design Evolution and Freeze Process for SMR-300 [5]. During this process the RWB and RAB were assessed together in a possible design alteration to include the RWB within the RAB. Based on this feedback gathered, the decision was elevated to the Design Decision Register [6] and brought in front of a larger team, to include Nuclear Island Systems, Projects, Balance of Plant, and Construction.

The evaluation team was tasked with preparing and answering internal challenges associated with normal operations, outage operations, construction costs, construction timelines, and RWB absorption without detrimental RAB layout disruption. After this information was assembled and reviewed, it was presented at a meeting with representatives from each of the SM Departments to review and consider any new and/or missing methodology, associated costs, implementation feasibility, any potential unforeseen effects on existing RAB layout or probabilistic risk evaluations, as well as the effect, if any, on the Limited Work Authorization (LWA) [1]. Questions and challenges were posed and answered based on a combination of the best available data, reasonable assumptions, and operational experience [8].

Table 2-1 lists the relevant requirements found in the SMR-300 Top Level Plant Design Requirements [4], a combination of both updated SMR-160 Objectives as well the relevant EPRI URD [3] requirements, that must be considered whether the waste processing facility is separate or absorbed by another structure.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The plant arrangement and building design features shall be defined to enhance the plant's capabilities to resist external threats of radiological sabotage.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The plant shall provide systems to store and manage the handling of liquid, gaseous, and solid radioactive waste and provide any necessary temporary storage. The best available technology shall be adopted. Storage capacity shall be at least: Liquid Radioactive Waste Capacity: 14 days or greater Solid Radioactive Waste Capacity: 30 days or greater

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The plant design shall include facilities and equipment to transfer spent fuel from wet storage to hardened (e.g. resistant to external conditions such as weather or missiles) dry storage casks located onsite and include adequate margin for temporary increases in the generation of such waste.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The capability to store six months or more production of low-level waste shall be provided.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The design shall provide adequate access space for maintenance, testing, operation, and component removal or replacement necessary to achieve plant design life.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The plant arrangement and the design of buildings shall provide for the control of personnel and movement of materials with a minimum of security and radiological control points to minimize security force requirements.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: Modularity concepts shall be applied to the design of systems and structures that are economical. The evaluation of economics shall consider the net impact on construction, including schedule, cost, and transportation logistics.

entries.section_title: Table 2-1: Top Level Plant List of Relevant Requirements
entries.text: The design and layout of SSCs shall maximize the efficiency of serial construction of multiple units by preferring the specification of identical arrangements, sizes, and orientations in the design of areas, systems, equipment, components, and bulk commodities. The use of mirroring shall be avoided to the extent practical.

3.1 Maintaining Current Building Arrangement
The first option is to keep the site layout and plot plan as is with the RWB as a standalone
building and only tied to the RAB via the mechanical process piping and electrical service
utilities. An initial building general arrangement was drafted and accounted for this on the Site
Layout. However, this option had several areas for improvement that are more fully discussed
under the application portions of Section 4.0, Considerations.

3.2 Incorporating the RWB into the RAB
By extending the RAB -38’ Elevation base mat approximately 57 ft to the plant North to
encompass the footprint of -21’ Elevation, the systems and functions of the RWB can be
contained within the RAB, thereby eliminating the entire RWB structure. This expansion of the
bottom elevation results in adding approximately 14,100 sq.ft. to the -38’ Elevation of the
Radiologically Controlled Area (RCA) of the RAB in lieu of the approximately 12,500 sq.ft. of the
RWB. This change also eliminates the separate base mat for the RWB and the -21’ Elevation of
the RAB, thereby creating one base mat for the RAB at -38’ Elevation. Lastly, the RAB will be
designed to include the systems and functions of the RWB and simplify their design at a
projected price that will be at least cost neutral if not cost advantageous.

4.1 Main Considerations
Several considerations factored into the option to incorporate the RWB. They stemmed from
the preliminary details that were determined for the RWB systems as well as the size of the
building. However, the considerations associated with ensuring no impact on nuclear safety or
upon the existing safety systems contained within the RAB was first and foremost.

4.1.1 Nuclear Safety
The consolidation of the liquid radioactive waste system within the lowest elevation of the RAB
enhanced safety as any flooding potential from any system tank rupture was limited once these
tanks were all moved to areas far from their previous areas. Additionally, it allowed for other systems to be routed from their previous areas for their consolidation thereby minimizing long
piping run. This will lead to better flooding and high energy line breaks (HELB) analysis due to
better placement and routing as well as the elimination of transferring both liquid and solid
waste between two separate buildings. Next, risks associated with cross-contamination of liquid
and solid waste unchanged as the associated systems continue to remain separate.
Furthermore, with this change, any liquids associated with severe accident conditions continue
to be processed via the LRW filter and demineralization system located on the 0’ Elevation of
the RAB instead of the 0’ Elevation of the RWB. This results in the dose impact on the Main
Control Room and/or the Remote Shutdown Facility to continue to remain unchanged. Finally,
many other aspects of the absorption-related changes were screened and discussed during
multiple RAB layout meetings to ensure the existing systems would still perform their intended

An initial Civil review between the three (3) base mats at -38’ of the RAB, -21’ of the RAB and 0’ of the RWB compared to the single RAB base mat at -38’ concluded that a single base mat was beneficial for seismic interaction and response, since buildings with separate base mats would result in relative displacements and accelerations, thus amplifying the seismic demand on connections between them. Combined building also provides better stability due to lower center-of-gravity to base aspect ratio. In addition, lowering the base mat elevations reduces the seismic demand on them. This also eliminates the requirement for isolation joints between the RCA and the MCR area of the RAB, and the RAB and the RWB.

The additional space on the lower elevation allows moving the Liquid Radioactive Waste (LRW) Holdup Tanks, currently on -21’ Elevation, to the bottom plant elevation. From an operational benefit, this promotes natural (gravity) drainage from the Radioactive Drain System (RDS) and simplifies water movement from Chemical and Volume Control System (CVC) Holdup Tanks on -38’ Elevation and Spent Resin Waste (SRW) transfer and disposal operations are relocated from the RWB to 0’ Elevation of the RAB, utilizing the open refueling area for these functions. Therefore, evolutions for LRW demineralizer and filter skid and disposal of SRW High Integrity Canisters (HICs) is unchanged.

A construction evaluation [7] shows approximately one-fifth the cost estimated is saved (also refer to Table 1-1, List of Assumptions, Assumption #1 and shortened timeline for the additional excavation of the RAB lower elevation compared to the construction of the RWB. The analysis included estimates for earth work, form work, reinforcement bar, concrete, foundation piling placement, and labor differences only (and none of the commodities).
The potential options mentioned above were further influenced by many other considerations that came out of multiple question and challenge meetings. Table 4-1 lists these other considerations.

entries.text: Both the mechanical and electrical Containment penetration areas have been expanded as a result of moving other rooms and equipment.
The risks associated with the Containment Penetrations being located below the flood area (-21' Elevation) have been minimized to the extent practical.
Easier placement of the Motor Control Centers, Power Panels, Distribution Panels, and Lighting Panels will occur as a result of moving other rooms and equipment.
Support design (e.g. cable trays) no longer has to take into consideration different building settling rates over plant life
The new design under the Control Building has allowed additional stairwells which now terminate on -38' Elevation that can be used for emergencies, overall improving egress pathways.
Elimination of the RWB allows for an additional truck bay access to the RAB which will allow one bay to support normal operations and one bay to support outage operations.
The Containment Building HVAC and Pressure Relief Systems can be located on 0' Elevation were they are better suited and maintained instead of located on 0' Elevation on top of the RAB Roof

entries.section_title: 14 Elimination of the Natural Phenomena and Internal/External Man-Induced Hazard Design Criteria for the RWB
entries.text: The RWB is an above ground structure classified as a RW-IIa (High Hazard) structure as per Regulatory Guide 1.143 [2]. Section 6.1 of the Reg Guide mandates the required studies and not having to perform any of these studies will save resources and result in a positive impact on Civil/Structural schedule. More specifically, the analyses eliminated include: wind, tornado, external missile impact, explosion, vehicle related events, and small aircraft impact.

entries.section_title: 15 Higher Elevation for the Volume Control Tank (VCT) [12, 14]
entries.text: The increased elevation of VCT provides for two critical operational considerations, margin for the Charging Pump Suction as well as prevention of inadvertent boric acid solution leakage into the Charging Pump suction during normal Boric Acid Storage Tank (BAST) recirculation and filtration.

The elimination of the separate RWB represents a net reduction of the overall volume of both radiative and non-radiative waste. More specifically, the six (6) sides of the building effectively translate to only four (4) when placed under the control building portion as the ceiling is already the floor above and the south wall is no longer required.

After further development of the feasibility and implementation of the RWB elimination and confirmation of the above action items being completed, a formal presentation of the design decision was made to the executive leadership team on August 29th, 2024.

The decision process concluded with no objections to the recommended design decision (unanimous decision) to consolidate the RWB functions into the expanded RAB, with executive concurrence to proceed.

entries.text: This specification provides the technical and quality requirements for the design and installation of a Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB) Crane for SMR lifting operations. The intent of this specification is to provide prospective Suppliers with the information necessary to prepare proposals for construction and installation of a RAB Crane in Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB) area.

This document provides specific design information relevant to the interfaces within the Reactor Auxiliary Building, operational requirements for the RAB Crane, specific operational features required by the Purchaser, and the major safety requirements as outlined in ASME NOG-1 [3.1.1].
The supplier/manufacturer is required to provide the RAB Crane in full compliance with ASME NOG-1 standards and all specifications outlined in this document.
RAB Crane is part of the fuel handling system. A detailed description of the requirements for this crane is described in Section 5 of this document.

This specification contains the phrase "To Be Determined" (TBD) in various sections. It is being released for preliminary cost proposals from Suppliers prior to the final design of significant interfaces within the RAB. Where TBD is indicated, the information may be either estimated or missing entirely. Suppliers should consider and annotate this when providing proposals for the RAB Crane described herein.

If the TBD information, especially the missing TBD information, significantly impacts pricing, this should be noted and explained in the proposal. In a future revision prior to the purchase of the RAB Crane, TBD will be replaced with final design information.

The current design of Reactor Auxiliary Building layout for the SMR is not yet finalized, and therefore the operational limit requirements for the RAB Crane cannot be fully verified at this stage. 5.3.1 The RAB Crane system is denoted as a Seismic Category II non-nuclear safety related with augmented quality requirements. The overhead bridge crane shall adhere to the design and safety criteria as Type II outlined in ASME NOG-1 [3.1.1]. Additionally, it should meet the applicable sections of design standards referenced within the specified standard, as well as the design criteria directed by this document.
5.3.2 Compliance with occupational safety and health standards for general industry as stated in Title 29, CFR, Part 1910.179 [3.1.16], is required.

5.3.3 Hoisting and travel machinery for the trolley and bridge, including wheels, axles, bearings, drives, gears, shafting, couplings, and brakes shall be designed and rated to handle all static and dynamic loads, including seismic loads, within allowable stress limits and allowable gear rating factors in accordance with the ASME NOG-1 [3.1.1].

5.3.4 The crane vendor's scope includes providing the loads imparted by the crane onto the runway rails and the runway/building structure, as well as performing a seismic evaluation. This evaluation shall account for both static and dynamic loads under full-load, partial-load, and unloaded crane conditions. Bounding accelerations and seismic criteria can be found in Appendix A.

5.3.5 The RAB Crane shall be designed to withstand the environmental conditions specified in Table 5-2 for the service life of the crane as stated in Table 5-1. Any components that require replacement due to the environmental conditions within the service life of the crane shall be documented in a separate procedure and schedule for replacing the components.

5.3.7 The design and installation of system components should facilitate testing and maintenance as outlined in the subsequent sections of this standard.

The auxiliary hoist shall be a wire rope hoist double reeved for true vertical lift.
The hoist motor shall be powered and controlled by a closed loop VFD and utilize sufficiently sized braking resistors for deceleration.
The auxiliary hoist shall be mounted on the same trolley as the main hoist.
Rail shall conform to all requirements set forth in the Specifications of the ASCE, AREA, AREA or any other commercial rolled sections with equivalent Specifications.
Rails shall be sized to accommodate the crane maximum wheel load, wheel diameter, and service class in accordance with ASME NOG-1 [3.1.1].
Rail attachment to the runway beams shall be approved by the Purchaser.
Sizing of the runway conductors shall be in accordance with NFPA 70 [3.1.13].
The runway conductors shall comprise of four insulated and finger-safe conductor bars for three-phase power, along with an earth conductor.
Dual collector shoes shall be used for each phase and earth conductor.
Runway conductors and mounting hardware shall be stainless steel.
The runway conductors shall receive power from a vendor-supplied manual disconnect positioned on the operating floor, easily accessible for the crane operator.

The primary operator interface shall be a remote radio control. The radio control transmitter shall include at a minimum, the following functions: Emergency Stop button that initiates an emergency stop for the RAB Crane. entries.text: The Supplier's quality assurance program must conform to the standards specified in ASME NOA-1, Part II3.1.151. Alternatively, if another quality assurance program has been agreed upon in the purchase contract, the Supplier must adhere to that program.

All personnel who will perform QA-related inspections, tests, and examinations of the contract shall be qualified and certified as per the Supplier's Quality Assurance Program requirements. Only qualified and certified auditors shall perform audits.
Certified Material Test Reports (CMTR) or alternative such as CoC are required for all structural components in the direct load path of the RAB Crane.
The Supplier shall create and retain documented evidence to demonstrate the requirements of this specification (codes, standards, regulatory guidance etc.).
Surface coating and painting shall be performed in accordance with ASME NOG-1, Section 3000 [3.1.1] and this specification.
The RAB Crane surface coating shall be Service Level II minimum in accordance with ASME NO-1-G, Section 3000 [3.1.1].
Equipment coating colors shall be approved by the Purchaser.

All crane coating applications shall be in accordance with the job specifications and procedures and the coating manufacturer's latest published instructions to the extent referenced in the job specification and procedures. Coatings work shall be inspected by coatings inspectors qualified and certified as required by ASME NOG-1 Section 3210(c) (NACE qualification or equal). The Supplier shall provide relevant certification and reports.
The factory-applied coatings on purchased items such as gearboxes, motors, etc. may remain "as is," provided they are suitable for the environmental conditions specified.
The following components or parts of components do not require the painting or the topcoat:
Crane and crane components marking shall be performed in accordance with ASME B30.2, Section 2-1.1 [3.1.2].
Crane nameplates with hoist capacities shall be furnished by the Supplier, with the rated load clearly visible on the crane.
Crane components and equipment nameplates shall contain all main necessary information (motors, gearboxes, electrical equipment, etc.).

Weights and centers-of-gravity shall be marked on major components. Where subassemblies are provided for site assembly, the weights and centers-of-gravity shall be indicated separately for each subassembly.

entries.text: 3.1 The applicable US codes and standards:
3.2 Reference Documents:
5.1 Reactor auxiliary building crane technical parameters (See Table 5-1)
5.2 Environmental characteristics
5.3 General design requirements
5.4 Electrical and control requirements
5.5 Material requirements
5.6 Safety requirements
5.7 Fabrication requirements

5.9 Maintenance requirements

This specification provides the technical and quality requirements for the design and installation of a Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB) Crane for SMR lifting operations. The intent of this specification is to provide prospective Suppliers with the information necessary to prepare proposals for construction and installation of a RAB Crane in Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB) area.

This document provides specific design information relevant to the interfaces within the Reactor Auxiliary Building, operational requirements for the RAB Crane, specific operational features required by the Purchaser, and the major safety requirements as outlined in ASME NOG-1 [3.1.1].
The supplier/manufacturer is required to provide the RAB Crane in full compliance with ASME NOG-1 standards and all specifications outlined in this document.
RAB Crane is part of the fuel handling system. A detailed description of the requirements for this crane is described in Section 5 of this document.
The RAB Crane is a Non-Safety Related with augmented quality requirements multipurpose lifting system that includes the following major components:

This specification contains the phrase "To Be Determined" (TBD) in various sections. It is being released for preliminary cost proposals from Suppliers prior to the final design of significant interfaces within the RAB. Where TBD is indicated, the information may be either estimated or missing entirely. Suppliers should consider and annotate this when providing proposals for the RAB Crane described herein.

entries.text: Three bi-directional joysticks designated for controlling hoisting, trolley, and bridge motions shall be provided. Each motion control shall offer either a minimum of 5 distinct speeds or provide infinitely variable speed settings.

Selector switches shall be provided to turn the main hoist, main trolley, auxiliary hoist, and auxiliary trolley on and off, allowing any combination of hoists and trolleys to operate simultaneously using the trolley and hoist joysticks.
A means to operate a jogging function for all lifting and travel functions.
The ability to control the crane lighting.
A secondary operator interface shall include at a minimum, the following:
Shall perform the same functions as the primary interface control.
A place for storing the secondary operator controller shall be provided on the bridge maintenance platform.

If the secondary operator interface is a pushbutton pendant, it shall hang from a festoon system that extends the full length of the bridge. The pendant cable shall have a quick disconnect to connect the pendant to the festoon trolley.

Travel Limit Switches & Travel Slow Down Switches shall be utilized at bridge and trolley end of travel. The travel slow down switch for the trolley and bridge shall only slow while traveling in the direction of the end stop.
The Main and Auxiliary Hoists shall have primary upper and lower rotary control limits switches as well as upper overtravel control limits switches.
The RAB Crane shall be equipped with the following lighting:

The crane shall be equipped with integrated LED lighting on the underside, providing a minimum illumination of 300-500 lux on the operating floor when ceiling-mounted lighting is blocked. The lights shall deliver a total of 7,000-10,000 lumens, evenly distributed, with a color temperature of 4000-5000K

The trolley shall be equipped with two LED spotlights, each providing 500-1000 lux of focused illumination around the hook area for enhanced visibility during lifting operations. The lights shall deliver 1,000-1,500 lumens each, with a color temperature of 4000-5000K. Mounted on adjustable brackets, the lights shall be positioned to avoid casting shadows and shall include anti-glare features.

The crane and trolley lights shall be dimmable utilizing 0-10V dimming, PWM dimming, or the option to turn off a portion of the fixtures for dimming, while maintaining adequate illumination for safe operations. The lighting shall be controlled using the crane radio control transmitter.
The electrical and control system shall be designed in accordance with the requirements of ASME NOG-1 [3.1.1] and NFPA 70 Article 610 [3.1.13].

The RAB Crane controls shall include a Three-Phase Line Voltage Monitor to provide protection against phase loss, phase reversal, voltage unbalance, and over/under voltage conditions of the input power.
Crane wireless remote control shall use licensed frequency radios in accordance with 47 CFR Part 90 [3.1.18].

All motor and brake controls shall be designed as fail-safe. If an electrical component were to fail, it would fail in a safe state. In the event that a fail-safe design cannot be implemented for specific components, redundancy may be implemented where required.

The RAB Crane bridge shall be grounded to a separate grounded runway conductor. All trolleys, motors, and electrical enclosures shall be grounded to the crane bridge by stranded, soft drawn bare copper wires that meet applicable NFPA 70, National Electrical Code [3.1.13] requirements.

The trolley frame shall be grounded to a separate feetoon wire terminated to a ground location on the RAB Crane bridge. All motors and electrical enclosures shall be grounded to the trolley frame by stranded, soft drawn bare copper wires that meet applicable NFPA 70, National Electrical Code [3.1.13] requirements.

All crane wiring shall be installed in intermediate galvanized metal conduit, except short lengths (three (3) ft. or less), to resistors, collectors, and motors where flexible seal tight conduit shall be used. The conduit system shall be supplied including all necessary fittings required to achieve adequate protection per NEMA [3.1.14] (see Table 5-6). Minimum NEMA [3.1.14] ratings shall be NEMA 12. Minimum IP ratings shall be IP54 [3.1.17].

Cable insulation and jacket materials shall be resistant to heat, moisture, impact, ozone, and nuclear radiation as required by the expected operating environment (see Table 5-2). PVC jacketed insulation shall not be used. Use of plastic tie wraps shall be minimized. Insulation and jacket materials shall be specifically selected to meet the requirements of the expected crane operating life, with consideration given to a possible plant life extension. See Table 5-1 for Crane operating life and possible extension of operating life.

entries.text: The auxiliary hoist shall be a wire rope hoist double reeved for true vertical lift.
The hoist motor shall be powered and controlled by a closed loop VFD and utilize sufficiently sized braking resistors for deceleration.
The auxiliary hoist shall be mounted on the same trolley as the main hoist.
Rail shall conform to all requirements set forth in the Specifications of the ASCE, AREA, AREA or any other commercial rolled sections with equivalent Specifications.
Rails shall be sized to accommodate the crane maximum wheel load, wheel diameter, and service class in accordance with ASME NOG-1 [3.1.1].
Rail attachment to the runway beams shall be approved by the Purchaser.
Sizing of the runway conductors shall be in accordance with NFPA 70 [3.1.13].
The runway conductors shall comprise of four insulated and finger-safe conductor bars for three-phase power, along with an earth conductor.
Dual collector shoes shall be used for each phase and earth conductor.
Runway conductors and mounting hardware shall be stainless steel.
The runway conductors shall receive power from a vendor-supplied manual disconnect positioned on the operating floor, easily accessible for the crane operator.

The primary operator interface shall be a remote radio control. The radio control transmitter shall include at a minimum, the following functions: Emergency Stop button that initiates an emergency stop for the RAB Crane. Momentary button that turns on an audible warning horn. Switch and button (or other means) to apply or remove power

Three bi-directional joysticks designated for controlling hoisting, trolley, and bridge motions shall be provided. Each motion control shall offer either a minimum of 5 distinct speeds or provide infinitely variable speed settings.

Selector switches shall be provided to turn the main hoist, main trolley, auxiliary hoist, and auxiliary trolley on and off, allowing any combination of hoists and trolleys to operate simultaneously using the trolley and hoist joysticks.
A means to operate a jogging function for all lifting and travel functions.
The ability to control the crane lighting.
A secondary operator interface shall include at a minimum, the following:
Shall perform the same functions as the primary interface control.
A place for storing the secondary operator controller shall be provided on the bridge maintenance platform.

If the secondary operator interface is a pushbutton pendant, it shall hang from a festoon system that extends the full length of the bridge. The pendant cable shall have a quick disconnect to connect the pendant to the festoon trolley.

Travel Limit Switches & Travel Slow Down Switches shall be utilized at bridge and trolley end of travel. The travel slow down switch for the trolley and bridge shall only slow while traveling in the direction of the end stop.
The Main and Auxiliary Hoists shall have primary upper and lower rotary control limits switches as well as upper overtravel control limits switches.
The RAB Crane shall be equipped with the following lighting:

The crane shall be equipped with integrated LED lighting on the underside, providing a minimum illumination of 300-500 lux on the operating floor when ceiling-mounted lighting is blocked. The lights shall deliver a total of 7,000-10,000 lumens, evenly distributed, with a color temperature of 4000-5000K

The trolley shall be equipped with two LED spotlights, each providing 500-1000 lux of focused illumination around the hook area for enhanced visibility during lifting operations. The lights shall deliver 1,000-1,500 lumens each, with a color temperature of 4000-5000K. Mounted on adjustable brackets, the lights shall be positioned to avoid casting shadows and shall include anti-glare features.

5.3.1 The RAB Crane system is denoted as a Seismic Category II non-nuclear safety related with augmented quality requirements. The overhead bridge crane shall adhere to the design and safety criteria as Type II outlined in ASME NOG-1 [3.1.1]. Additionally, it should meet the applicable sections of design standards referenced within the specified standard, as well as the design criteria directed by this document.
5.3.2 Compliance with occupational safety and health standards for general industry as stated in Title 29, CFR, Part 1910.179 [3.1.16], is required.

5.3.3 Hoisting and travel machinery for the trolley and bridge, including wheels, axles, bearings, drives, gears, shafting, couplings, and brakes shall be designed and rated to handle all static and dynamic loads, including seismic loads, within allowable stress limits and allowable gear rating factors in accordance with the ASME NOG-1 [3.1.1].

5.3.4 The crane vendor's scope includes providing the loads imparted by the crane onto the runway rails and the runway/building structure, as well as performing a seismic evaluation. This evaluation shall account for both static and dynamic loads under full-load, partial-load, and unloaded crane conditions. Bounding accelerations and seismic criteria can be found in Appendix A.

5.3.5 The RAB Crane shall be designed to withstand the environmental conditions specified in Table 5-2 for the service life of the crane as stated in Table 5-1. Any components that require replacement due to the environmental conditions within the service life of the crane shall be documented in a separate procedure and schedule for replacing the components.
5.3.6 The crane service class shall be as stated in Table 5-1 and in accordance with CMAA 70 [3.1.3].
5.3.7 The design and installation of system components should facilitate testing and maintenance as outlined in the subsequent sections of this standard.
5.3.8 Clearances between the installed crane and permanent building structures

entries.text: General Description and Operating Conditions
The Stud Tensioners and associated power unit will be used to elongate the SMR-300 reactor vessel closure studs a predetermined amount necessary to establish the required flange loading.

Depending on tensioner design and number of tensioners used, the studs may be tensioned simultaneously or in groups using the number of passes required according to an established programming procedure.
Normal ambient temperature and pressure conditions will exist during tensioning operations.
The Stud Tensioning System shall be suitable for interfacing with the fastener type as defined in Table 1 below and Attachment 9.1 of this purchase specification.
The Stud Tensioning System shall be capable of achieving the parameters as defined in Table 1 below.

The Tensioners shall be designed for normal operation in a vertical position. Handling fixtures (on the Tensioners) shall be located so that the tensioner hangs free in a position such that a vertical line through the center of the puller bar and puller bar socket, coincides with the vertical axis of the closure stud at the time of engagement with the closure stud and during subsequent tensioning.

The Puller Bar and puller bar socket shall be counterbalanced in such a manner that their (combined) weight is not transmitted to the closure stud threads during initial engagement of the puller bar socket and closure stud. It is desirable that a light downward force should be exerted manually to effect engagement between puller bar socket and closure stud.
Hydraulic connections shall be designed to make incorrect connections impossible (preferred), or for hydraulic hoses to be clearly identified to ensure connections are made correctly.
For Stud Tensioning Systems operated hydraulically, the following shall be provided by the vendor:
The Stud Tensioning System shall have minimal traps for particulate that could make it difficult to clean.

Materials used for construction of the tensioners and power unit should be selected for their proper relation with other materials. Consideration should be given to galling, corrosion, erosion, wear, and other conditions associated with materials application.

The Stud Tensioning System is used in an environment where contamination is possible. The equipment may become contaminated. Design features should ensure that the equipment can be effectively cleaned and maintained after being used in radiologically contaminated areas, reducing the potential for contamination spread and improving safety during maintenance activities.

entries.text: This specification covers the general requirements for design performance, manufacture, testing and packing for shipment of a reactor vessel Stud Tensioning system.
1.1 Equipment and Services to be Furnished by the Supplier
1.1.1 Three or more completely assembled vertically oriented Stud Tensioner units. Each unit to consist generally of the basic parts described below:
Hydraulic cylinder or cylinders
Hydraulic piston or pistons with necessary seals
Air operated piston return system as required.
Positive overstroke prevention device
Reactor vessel stud nut tightening device.
Housing for tightening device drive sleeve and other parts as required.
Handwheel to operate puller bar and socket.
Provisions for lifting tensioners.
Counterbalance springs

1.1.2 One (completely assembled) Portable Power Unit (on wheels) to supply Hydraulic Pressure simultaneously to the Tensioners consisting of an air operated Hydraulic Pump, Air Regulator, Air Filter and Water Trap, Air Line Oiler, Air Safety Valve, Hydraulic Release Valve, Air Operating Valve, Oil Reservoir, Air Gage, Muffler, and Associated Piping and Fittings.
Where required by Supplier's design, the power unit may be electrically driven, and may be combined with the tensioner.
1.1.3 One Stud Elongation Measuring Rod and Dial Indicator or equal for each tensioner.
1.1.4 Hydraulic and Pneumatic Hoses and Fittings for interconnecting the Tensioners to each other and to the power unit.
1.1.5 Recommended Spare Parts.
1.1.6 Documentation as specified elsewhere in the specification.

Drawings and specifications
Material certifications
This specification covers the general requirements for design performance, manufacture, testing and packing for shipment of a reactor vessel Stud Tensioning system.

Hydraulic cylinder or cylinders
Hydraulic piston or pistons with necessary seals
Air operated piston return system as required.
Positive overstroke prevention device
Reactor vessel stud nut tightening device.
Housing for tightening device drive sleeve and other parts as required.
Handwheel to operate puller bar and socket.

Counterbalance springs

1.1.2 One (completely assembled) Portable Power Unit (on wheels) to supply Hydraulic Pressure simultaneously to the Tensioners consisting of an air operated Hydraulic Pump, Air Regulator, Air Filter and Water Trap, Air Line Oiler, Air Safety Valve, Hydraulic Release Valve, Air Operating Valve, Oil Reservoir, Air Gage, Muffler, and Associated Piping and Fittings.
Where required by Supplier's design, the power unit may be electrically driven, and may be combined with the tensioner.
1.1.3 One Stud Elongation Measuring Rod and Dial Indicator or equal for each tensioner.

entries.text: Independence shall be maintained between the organization(s) performing the checking (quality assurance and control) functions and the organizations performing the functions. This provision is not applicable to design review/verification nor in certain applications where individuals within a specific organization did not perform the specific work and are appropriately qualified.
In establishing its organizational structure, Holtec commits to compliance with NQA-1-2015 Part 1, Requirement 1.

Holtec International has established the necessary measures and governing procedures to implement the SMR LLC QAP TR as described in the HQAM. Holtec International is committed to implementing the SMR LLC QAP TR in all aspects of work that are important to safety (to include safety-related) as described and to the extent delineated herein. The SMR LLC QAP TR includes monitoring activities against acceptance criteria in a manner sufficient to provide assurance that the activities important to safety (to include safety-related) are performed satisfactorily.

The objective of the SMR LLC QAP TR is to assure that Holtec International's processes and activities as delineated in Table 1.1 are in accordance with governing regulations and license requirements. The program is based on the requirements set forth in the codes and standards identified in Table 1.1.2 of this document and as further described in this SMR LLC QAP TR. The SMR LLC QAP TR applies to those quality-related activities that involve the functions of safety-related structures, systems, and components (SSCs) associated with the processes and activities identified in Table 1.1.1. Holtec International established and maintains a plant-level SSC classification listing of all safety-related SSCs and non-safety related SSCs that are significant contributors to plant safety. A list or system that identifies SSCs and activities to which this program applies is maintained at Holtec International facilities. Cost and scheduling challenges must be addressed; however, they do not prevent proper implementation of the SMR LLC QAP TR.

The SMR LLC QAP TR provides for the planning and accomplishment of activities affecting quality under suitably controlled conditions. Controlled conditions include the use of appropriate analytical tools, suitable environmental conditions for accomplishing the activity, and assurance that prerequisites for the given activity have been satisfied. The SMR LLC QAP TR provides for any special controls, processes, test equipment, tools, and skills to attain the required quality and for verification of that quality.

As described in Part III of the SMR LLC QAP TR, specific program controls are applied to non-safety related SSCs that are significant contributors to plant safety, for which the codes listed in Table 1.1.2 are not applicable. The specific program controls, consistent with applicable sections of the SMR LLC QAP TR, are applied to those SSCs in a select manner, targeted at those characteristics or critical attributes that qualifies an SSC as a significant contributor to plant safety.

Delegated responsibilities may be performed under a supplier's or principal contractor's QAP, provided that the supplier or principal contractor has been approved as a supplier in accordance with the SMR LLC QAP TR. Periodic audits and assessments of supplier QA programs are performed to assure compliance with the supplier's or principal contractor's QAP and that quality expectations are met. In addition, routine interfaces with the supplier's personnel provide added assurance that quality procedures are met.

Except where noted in other sections of the SMR LLC QAP TR, a grace period of 90 days may be applied to provisions that are required to be performed on a periodic basis. Annual evaluations and audits that must be performed on a triennial basis are examples where the 90-day general period could be applied. The grace period does not allow the "clock" for a particular activity to be reset forward. The "clock" for an activity is reset backwards by performing the activity early. Audit schedules are based on the month in which the audit starts.

Further, Holtec International ensures through the systematic process described herein that its suppliers of safety-related items and services meet the applicable requirements of 10CFR50 Appendix B except where Holtec International performs commercial grade dedication or implements applicable portions of its own HQAM on the supplier.

entries.text: Holtec International has established the necessary measures and governing procedures to demonstrate that items will perform satisfactorily in service. The test program includes, as appropriate, proof tests prior to installation, construction tests and preoperational tests. Test programs include criteria for determining when testing is required in order to demonstrate that performance of an item or items is in accordance with design. Tests are performed according to procedures that include, as applicable and consistent with the effect on safety: (1) instructions and prerequisites to perform the tests, (2) use of proper test equipment, (3) acceptance criteria, (4) mandatory verification points as necessary to confirm satisfactory test completion, (5) any special qualification requirements for personnel and (6) any special environmental conditions.

Test results are documented and reviewed to assure that the test requirements have been satisfied. Test records are traceable to the item(s) tested. If acceptance criteria are not met, re-testing is performed as needed to confirm acceptability following correction of the item deficiencies that caused the failure.

Test records, at a minimum and as applicable, shall identify the item tested, date of test, tester or data recorder, type of observation, results and acceptability, action taken in connection with any deviations noted, and the person evaluating the test results.
Tests are performed and results documented in accordance with applicable technical and regulatory requirements.

Holtec International establishes and implements provisions to assure that computer programs used in applications affecting safety are prepared, documented, verified, and tested, and used such that the expected output is obtained, and configuration control maintained. Procedures are in place to address controls for both Holtec International-generated computer programs and computer programs Holtec International-purchased.

In establishing testing requirements, Holtec International commits to compliance with NQA-1-2015, Part 1, Requirement 11 and NQA-1-2015 Part 2, Subpart 2.7 "Quality Assurance Requirements for Computer Software for Nuclear Facility Applications".

Holtec International has established the necessary measures and governing procedures to control the calibration, maintenance, and use of M&TE that are used for activities affecting quality. The provisions of such procedures cover equipment such as tools, gages, and instruments. Appropriate documentation will be maintained for M&TE to indicate the control status, when the next calibration is due, and identify any limitations on use of the M&TE. Calibration records that are traceable to the specific M&TE shall provide results of calibration.

M&TE are calibrated at prescribed intervals, or prior to use, against certified equipment having known valid relationships to nationally recognized standards. If no nationally recognized standards exist, the basis for calibration is documented.

Procedures also address requirements for control and evaluation of out of calibration conditions. A calibration is performed when the accuracy of the equipment is suspect. When measuring and test equipment is lost, damaged, or found to be out-of-calibration, the validity of previous measurement, inspection, or test results, and the acceptability of items previously inspected or tested, shall be evaluated.
Calibration and control measures are not required for rulers, tape measures, levels, and other similar devices, if normal commercial equipment provides adequate accuracy.
In establishing provisions for control of measuring and test equipment, Holtec International commits to compliance with NQA-1-2015, Part 1, Requirement 12.

entries.text: In establishing provisions for records, Holtec commits to compliance with NQA-1-2015, Part 1, Requirement 17, and regulatory positions stated in Regulatory Guide RG 1.28 Rev 5.

Holtec International has established the necessary measures and governing procedures to implement audits to verify that activities covered by the SMR LLC QAP TR are performed in conformance with the established requirements. The audit programs are themselves reviewed for effectiveness as a part of the overall audit process.

Internal audits of the implementation of SMR LLC QAP TR are performed with a frequency commensurate with the relative importance of the activity being audited. Internal audits are performed to verify compliance and effectiveness of implementation of programs and procedures. Internal audits also provide a means to verify that processes and programs are meaningful and comply with the overall SMR LLC QAP TR.

The audits are scheduled in a manner to provide coverage and coordination with ongoing activities, based on the status and importance of the activity and to assure that each applicable element of the SMR LLC QAP TR is audited at least once each year or at least once during the life of the activity, whichever is shorter. Additional audits may be performed as deemed necessary by management. Audit results are provided to responsible management.

Audits of suppliers, when required, are conducted as described in this section and also under Part II, Section 7. An audit is initially performed after the supplier has completed sufficient work to demonstrate that its organization is implementing a QA Program. Where sufficient work has not yet been completed, an initial programmatic audit may occur to verify the QA Program adequately addresses QA requirements and a follow up implementation audit may be performed when sufficient work has occurred.

If a subsequent contract or a contract modification significantly enlarges the scope of or changes the methods or controls for activities performed by the same supplier, an audit of the modified requirements is conducted, thus starting a new triennial period.

Audits are conducted by trained personnel not having direct responsibilities in the area being audited and in accordance with preplanned and approved audit plans or checklists, under the direction of a qualified lead auditor. Audit reports are generated. Any audit findings are identified and follow up action is performed to verify appropriate corrective actions have been implemented.

In establishing the independent audit program, Holtec commits to compliance with NQA-1-2015, Part 1, Requirement 18 with the following exceptions: ASME NQA-1-2015, Part 1 Requirement 18 Section 200, states that, "A grace period of 90 days may be applied to scheduled audits and annual evaluations of supplier performance." As discussed in Section 7, Subsection 7.1, "A grace period not to exceed 25 percent of the audit or survey interval shall be allowed under exigent conditions." Further details related to this increased grace period are provided in Part II, Section 7.

entries.text: Holtec International has established qualification programs for personnel performing quality inspections. The qualification program requirements are described in Part II, Section 2.0.
In establishing inspection requirements, Holtec International commits to compliance with NQA-1-2015. Part 1, Requirement 10. See exceptions under Part II, Section 7.0.

Holtec International has established the necessary measures and governing procedures to demonstrate that items will perform satisfactorily in service. The test program includes, as appropriate, proof tests prior to installation, construction tests and preoperational tests. Test programs include criteria for determining when testing is required in order to demonstrate that performance of an item or items is in accordance with design. Tests are performed according to procedures that include, as applicable and consistent with the effect on safety: (1) instructions and prerequisites to perform the tests, (2) use of proper test equipment, (3) acceptance criteria, (4) mandatory verification points as necessary to confirm satisfactory test completion, (5) any special qualification requirements for personnel and (6) any special environmental conditions.

Test results are documented and reviewed to assure that the test requirements have been satisfied. Test records are traceable to the item(s) tested. If acceptance criteria are not met, re-testing is performed as needed to confirm acceptability following correction of the item deficiencies that caused the failure.

Test records, at a minimum and as applicable, shall identify the item tested, date of test, tester or data recorder, type of observation, results and acceptability, action taken in connection with any deviations noted, and the person evaluating the test results.
Tests are performed and results documented in accordance with applicable technical and regulatory requirements.

Holtec International establishes and implements provisions to assure that computer programs used in applications affecting safety are prepared, documented, verified, and tested, and used such that the expected output is obtained, and configuration control maintained. Procedures are in place to address controls for both Holtec International-generated computer programs and computer programs Holtec International-purchased.

In establishing testing requirements, Holtec International commits to compliance with NQA-1-2015, Part 1, Requirement 11 and NQA-1-2015 Part 2, Subpart 2.7 "Quality Assurance Requirements for Computer Software for Nuclear Facility Applications".

entries.text: Holtec International's Nuclear Quality Assurance Manual (HQAM) is the top-level policy document that establishes the quality assurance program and policy and assigns major functional responsibilities for important to safety (to include safety-related) activities conducted by or for Holtec International. The HQAM describes the methods and establishes quality assurance and administrative control requirements that meet the applicable codes and standards.

The Holtec International Quality Assurance Program (HQAP) is defined by the Holtec International HQAM (which describes the QA elements) along with the associated implementing documents such as procedures. Procedures and instructions that control Holtec International's activities related to quality are required to be developed prior to commencement of those activities. Policies establish high-level responsibilities and authority for carrying out important administrative functions which are outside the scope of the HQAP. Procedures establish practices for certain activities which are common to all Holtec International organizations performing those activities so that the activity is controlled and carried out in a manner that meets HQAP requirements. Procedures specific to a site, organization, or group establish detailed implementation requirements and methods and may be used to implement policies or be unique to particular functions or work activities.

This SMR, LLC Quality Assurance Program Topical Report (SMR LLC QAPTR) provides a summary of the requirements set forth within the HQAP related to design, fabrication, construction, and testing activities necessary for Holtec's SMR. Holtec International (synonymous with Holtec) is used throughout this SMR LLC QAPTR as the organization responsible for the execution of the quality assurance activities.

This SMR LLC QAPTR contains programmatic requirements that mirror and amplify the provisions of 10CFR50 Appendix B for applicable related to design, fabrication, construction, and testing activities, pursuant to a 10CFR50 Construction Permit Application and/or Limited Work Authorization. The SMR LLC QAPTR has been specifically established to serve as the primary vehicle to describe the control of all important to safety (to include safety-related) activities carried out by Holtec International for activities listed in Table I.1.1 and under the rules of the codes and standards identified in Table I.1.2 under a seamless quality regimen.

Each of the programmatic commitments in this SMR LLC QAPTR are elaborated as actionable instructions in implementing procedures called Holtec Quality Procedures (HQPs), Holtec Standard Procedures (HSPs), and other supporting procedures and instructions.

Safety-related structures, systems, or components (SSCs), under the control of this SMR LLC QAPTR, are identified by design documents. The technical aspects of these SSCs are considered when determining program applicability, including, as appropriate, the SSC's design safety function.

The policy of Holtec International is to assure a high degree of availability and reliability of the nuclear plant(s) and supporting equipment while ensuring the health and safety of all nuclear workers and the general public. To this end, selected elements of the SMR LLC QAPTR are also applied to certain activities that are not safety-related, but support safe, economic, and reliable plant operations, or where other NRC guidance establishes quality assurance requirements.
The SMR LLC QAP includes, but is not limited to, the following primary processes related to the design and construction of SMR's:
Engineering Design Procurement Fabrication Construction Inspection and Testing Training and Qualification
(The SMR LLC QAP complies with the following codes and standards)

Code of Federal Regulations Miscellaneous Codes and Standards 10CFR21, 10CFR50 Appendix B ASME NQA-1-2015 Part 1 with exceptions as listed in the applicable criteria of this SMR LLC QAP TR. Applicable subparts from Part 2 of ASME NQA-1-2015 as listed in each section within this SMR LLC QAP TR and with exceptions/clarifications as listed in the applicable section of this SMR LLC QAP TR.

entries.text: Holtec International has established the necessary measures and governing procedures to control the handling, storage, packaging, shipping, cleaning, and preservation of items to prevent inadvertent damage or loss, and to prevent deterioration. These provisions include specific procedures, when required, to maintain acceptable quality of safety-related items.

Items are appropriately marked and labeled during packaging, shipping, handling, and storage to identify, maintain, and preserve the item's integrity and indicate the need for special controls. Special controls (such as containers, shock absorbers, accelerometers, inert gas atmospheres, specific moisture content levels, and temperature levels) are provided when required to maintain acceptable quality.

Cleanliness controls for work on safety-related and risk-significant non-safety related equipment are required to be established that minimize the introduction of foreign material and maintain system/component cleanliness throughout maintenance or modification activities. Procedures require documented verification of absence of foreign material prior to system closure.

Special or additional handling, storage, shipping, cleaning, and preservation requirements are identified and implemented as specified in procurement documents and applicable procedures. Where special requirements are specified, the items and containers (where used) are suitably marked.

Special handling tools and equipment are used and controlled as necessary to ensure safe and adequate handling. Special handling tools and equipment are inspected and tested in accordance with procedures at specified time intervals or prior to use. Operators of special handling and lifting equipment are experienced or trained, as appropriate, in the use of the equipment. Where required, Holtec complies with applicable hoisting, rigging and transportation regulations and codes.
Provisions are described for the storage of chemicals, reagents (including control of shelf life), lubricants, and other consumable materials.

In establishing provisions for handling, storage, packaging and shipping, Holtec International commits to compliance with NQA-1-2015, Part 1, Requirement 13, and Subpart 2.1, "Quality Assurance Requirements for Cleaning of Fluid Systems and Associated Components for Nuclear Facilities," Subpart 2.2, "Quality Assurance Requirements for Packaging, Shipping, Receiving, Storage, and Handling of Items for Nuclear Facilities," and Subpart 2.3, "Quality Assurance Requirements for Housekeeping at Nuclear Facilities."

Holtec International has established the necessary measures and governing procedures to identify the inspection, test, and operating status of items in order to ensure that required inspections and tests are performed and to ensure that items that have not passed the required inspections and tests are not inadvertently installed, used, operated, or shipped. These measures also establish the necessary authorities and controls for the application and removal of status indicators or labels.

Suitable marking methods such as tags, stamps, labels, or travelers are used to identify the test or inspection status of an item. Status may also be indicated by physical location such as a designated hold area.

In addition, temporary design changes (temporary modifications), such as temporary bypass lines, electrical jumpers, and lifted wires, and temporary trip-point settings, are controlled by procedures that include requirements for appropriate installation and removal, independent/concurrent verifications, and status tracking.

Maintenance or modifications which may affect functioning of safety-related SSCs shall be performed in a manner to ensure quality at least equivalent to that specified in original design bases and requirements, materials specifications and inspection requirements.
In establishing provisions for inspection, test and operating status, Holtec International commits to compliance with NQA-1-2015, Part 1, Requirement 14.

entries.text: Holtec International has established the necessary measures and governing procedures to control items, including services, that do not conform to specified requirements to prevent inadvertent installation or use. Controls provide for identification, documentation, evaluation, segregation when practical, and disposition of nonconforming items, and for notification to affected organizations.
Nonconforming items are segregated and/or tagged and/or otherwise identified until such time as disposition of the condition is completed and appropriate actions, as applicable, are taken.

Nonconformances are corrected or resolved prior to relying on the item to perform its intended safety function. Items that are reworked or repaired are inspected and tested, as appropriate, with the original inspection and test requirements or specified alternatives.

Nonconformances are evaluated for impact to assure that the final condition does not adversely affect safety, operation, or maintenance of the item or service. Nonconformances to design requirements dispositioned as repair or use-as-is are subject to design control measures commensurate with those applied to the original design. Technical justification for the acceptability of a nonconforming item, dispositioned as use-as-is or repair shall be documented. Nonconformance dispositions are performed by personnel that have a) competence in the specific area they are evaluating; b) an adequate understanding of the requirements; and c) access to pertinent background information.

10CFR21 (for construction, 10CFR50.55(e) applies) is considered to apply to those items and services identified as safety-related. 10CFR21 (for construction, 10CFR50.55(e) applies) reportability is evaluated for each applicable nonconformance.
In establishing measures for controls for nonconforming materials, parts, or components, Holtec International commits to compliance with NQA-1-2015, Part 1, Requirement 15.

Holtec International has established the necessary measures and governing procedures to promptly identify, control, document, classify, and correct conditions adverse to quality. Holtec procedures require all personnel to identify known conditions adverse to quality. Holtec procedures assure that significant conditions adverse to quality are documented into Holtec's corrective action program in order to allow for identification of cause and determination of actions to prevent recurrence. Completed actions are verified. Significant conditions adverse to quality, significant adverse trends, the cause of the condition, the corrective actions taken are documented and reported to responsible management.

In the case of suppliers working on safety-related activities, Holtec International may delegate specific responsibilities for corrective actions but Holtec International maintains responsibility for the effectiveness of corrective action measures.

10CFR21 (for construction, 10CFR50.55(e) applies) is considered to apply to those items and services identified as safety-related. 10CFR21 (for construction, 10CFR50.55(e) applies) reportability is evaluated for each condition that is adverse to quality.
In establishing provisions for corrective action, Holtec commits to compliance with NQA-1- 2015, Part 1 Requirement 16.
