entries.text: Elevation -0’-0’’ Cable Routing Notes: 1.) Per EPRI LURD (Chapter 11, section 2.6.3.9. Cables shall be routed to avoid harsh environments to the extent practical. Harsh environments include high temperature, high radiation, areas subject to chemical exposure, and wet areas. This includes macro environments such as steam tunnels, and micro environments such as in close proximity to hot pipes or valves. 2.) N1E cables shall not be routed in the same electrical raceway as DIV-A or DIV-B cables. 3.) entries.text: The purpose of this report is to provide guidance and establish a practice for the application and installation of cable routing for the electric distribution within the SMR-300. This report focusses on the two unit design of the RAB.

This report proposes a preliminary routing of the electrical distribution system which includes the Class 1E (Safety related) Division A (DIV-A), Class 1E Division B (DIV-B) and Non-class 1E (N1E) circuits from the respective switchgears (SWG) present in the electrical room. The electrical room is outside the RAB, the Safety related and N1E cables penetrate the RAB through the south side of the RAB to the respective rooms as shown in Section 8.0. As some rooms are shared between both units it is important to maintain appropriate separation between the Class 1E Divisions. Additionally, this report references the applicable circuit separation requirements from the SMR-300 design standard for grouping and separation [1]. Hence, this report will help ensure that the separation requirements are met during preparation of the detailed cable trays or conduit design and help in detailed routing which will be designed in SmartPlant or similar design software. This report is not intended to determine the number of conduits or cable trays that will be required, or to assign cables to their respective raceways, but rather to show proposed routes that would assist in maintaining adequate separation between DIV-A, DIV-B and N1E circuits.

The following abbreviations are specific to this document. For other acronyms or terms not listed here consult the SMR-300 Acronyms, and Glossary of Terms [2] and the Numbering, Coding, Tagging, and Plant Breakdown Structure [3].
COM Communication System
CRD Control Rod Drive Mechanism
CS Containment Structure
DBE Design Basis Event
DCE DC Power Distribution System
EMI Electromagnetic Interference
EPA Electrical Penetration Assembly
FPP Fire Protection Program

entries.text: This report is to document the methodology, and decisions made with regards to cable routing in the Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB) of the SMR-300. The cable routing is intended to assist with the location of major equipment and the required raceways conduits and wall penetrations to support power distribution. This report provides a visual representation of the power distribution network within the RAB using two unit configuration and can be used for a detailed cable tray and conduit routing in SmartPlant or similar design software.

This report only focusses on power distribution and not instrumentation routing. Instrumentation cables are multiconductor cables used to transmit low-energy (power-limited) electrical signals with low voltage levels (less than 130 V) and relatively low current levels between equipment (usually electronic, such as monitors and analyzers) and control equipment for apparatus. The Plant Lighting System (PLS) cable routing was not considered or included in this report.

The cable penetration into the DIV-B electrical room and DIV-A electrical room is on

Table 5-1 summarizes all the starting and finishing points of the electrical distribution, which was developed from the General Arrangement of RAB for SMR-300 [10]. The SMR-300 design standard for grouping and separation report [1] was used to define the separation criteria between DIV-A, DIV-B and N1E cable routes. This report provides the basis for the separation distances that are listed in Section 8.0. Cable routing for major power distribution and the associated pathways of the RAB are referenced in Section 8.0 of this report.

Based on the current cable routing in the RAB, the cable penetration will be on +20 feet on elevation 0’-0” and run down to elevation -21’-0” in the non-safety cable spreading room, this will help to avoid any interference with the overhead cranes on elevation 0’-0”, please see assumption 3 in section 4.0.
There are no cable routes in the radiologically controlled area on elevation 0’-0” due to possible heavy traffic of equipment and overhead crane.

The RAB has dedicated rooms/areas for different systems of Unit 1 and Unit 2 respectively for SMR-300, some rooms are shared between both units. These rooms have equipment which interact with a number of electrical systems including but not necessarily limited to the MVE, LVE, ICE, DCE, and COM systems. The cables associated with each electrical distribution system generally vary in size (gauge or diameter), insulation type, conductor type and number of conductors per cable depending on what equipment is being supported. Generally, communications and low voltage cables are not routed together with medium voltage cables in the same electrical pathway. Final cable routing and raceway design should also consider other factors such as the potential effects of nearby EM and RFI sources, the number of fire areas a cable is passing through, the types of cables that are passing through a fire area, and hazards and interferences that are present in each room.

The methodology used in this report does not attempt to define specific raceways to be used by the various cables, nor does it attempt to consider the aforementioned factors; rather, the methodology used in this report is focused on the following:
Identifying all major rooms/equipment in the RAB that are specific to a Safety division, DIV-A and DIV-B or N1E and what electrical distribution system they will be interacting with.
Identifying which rooms/components are associated with (Unit 1 or Unit 2)
Minimizing cable routing in high radiation areas.
Avoiding routing Division A, Division B and or non-safety cables together where possible.
Optimizing the cable routes by using existing rooms and walls.
Avoid cables running from/through the Radwaste Building
Identifying areas where cables can be routed up or down on different elevations in the RAB.
When preparing this report, the following process was followed:
General Arrangement of Reactor Auxiliary Building for SMR-300 [10] was reviewed to understand the layout of the RAB and location of the different rooms/systems.

The rooms/equipment which were specific to DIV-A, DIV-B or N1E were listed in the Microsoft Excel file "RAB Cable Routes.xlsx" with key attributes such as electrical division, voltage level, interfacing equipment and respective electrical distribution system. Additionally, each identified room/equipment was given a unique number to use that as an identifier in the routing drawing shown in Section 8.0. The excel sheet also gives detailed information of the routes in the remarks section and if the respective route is shown on the routing drawing as some interfacing equipment can be in the same room.
Avoided routing DIV-A, DIV-B and or N1E cables together where possible.
Identified the potential areas where the cables can be routed up through the ceiling or down through the floor and kept these routes close to the wall.

entries.text: All technical specifications provided by the Supplier to the Buyer, including but not limited to dimensions, weights, volumes, and other relevant measurements, shall be provided in the Imperial System of units (e.g., inches, feet, pounds, gallons, etc.).
The Supplier may perform its calculations and procurement activities using the International System of Units (SI), but all results reported to the Buyer shall be converted to Imperial System units.
Where applicable, dual units (Imperial and SI) may be provided in the Buyer's records, but the Imperial units must be the primary units and be clearly indicated.
Supplier provided documentation, such as user manuals, maintenance guides, and safety instructions, must be provided in English.
Any diagrams, charts, or tables must use Imperial System units primarily.
The Supplier must comply with these requirements as part of their contractual obligations.
The requirements in this section shall also apply to all Sub-Suppliers.
Non-compliance with the language and measurement unit requirements above may result in penalties, rejection of goods or documents, or termination of the contract.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: 14.1 RCP Design Code and Design Parameters

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: The SMR-300 RCPs shall be designed, fabricated, inspected, and tested in full compliance with the 2021 edition of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Code Section III, Division 1, Subsection NB for Class 1 components.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Each pump shall meet the following requirements:

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Service Levels: The pump shall be capable of sustaining operational loads and stresses corresponding to Service Levels A (Normal), B (Upset), C (Emergency), and D (Faulted).

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Stress Evaluation: Stress limits for the overall pump assembly (i.e., casing and nozzles) shall comply with Subsection NB for all postulated conditions thereby ensuring an adequate safety margin against all primary, secondary, and peak stresses. Fatigue evaluations must confirm cyclic load resistance.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Material Requirements: Materials shall meet NB-2000 specifications, including certification and traceability requirements.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Design Criteria: The pump design shall conform to NB-3400 (Pump Design), NB-3500 (Valve Design), and NB-3600 (Piping Design), as applicable. Supports and connections must meet Subsection NF (2021 Edition).

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Seismic and Accident Conditions: The pump shall withstand seismic loads and other dynamic forces without functional failure under Service Level D conditions.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Fabrication and Quality Assurance: Fabrication, installation, examination, and testing shall adhere to NB-4000, NB-5000, and NB-6000 to ensure the integrity of all pressure boundaries and welds.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Documentation and Certification: All documentation, including certified material test reports (CMTRs), design calculations, and inspection records, shall comply with Subsection NB requirements for Class 1 components.

entries.section_title: 14.2 Design Requirements for Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The Holtec SMR-300 RCPs shall meet all the following general and specific design requirements. These requirements are all listed in order of importance.

Pumps are expected to normally only pump single phase flow (i.e., compressed water) at NOP/NOT. However, during accident conditions (e.g., a sudden RCS system pressure decrease), and possibly during normal start-up and shut-down, two-phase flow conditions may occur. These two-phase flow conditions may result in flashing and vapor (steam) formation in the pump casings. Pump design shall be robust in order to prevent pump damage from the potential vibration and shock of hydraulic surges that may occur during temporary two-phase flow conditions. Pump design robustness in the case of two-phase flows should specifically address areas such as:

Two-phase flow conditions are only expected to occur during Design Basis Accident (DBA) conditions such as medium to large LOCA or a Main Steam Line Break (MSLB). These events are not expected to occur during the life of the plant. The RCP will not be operated during or following DBAs and is therefore not required to be designed by the Supplier to operate during these periods.

During RCP start-up, localized two-phase flow can occur around the pump vanes due to cavitation if the pump operates close to the vapor pressure of the coolant. The RCP is most susceptible to cavitation at startup due to low RCS system pressures while performing heat-up operations, potentially resulting in inadequate net positive suction head (NPSH). The Supplier shall ensure adequate NPSH requirements to prevent pump internals damage.

It is important for reactor protection purposes that the reactor coolant continues to flow for a short and well-defined time after a loss of pump motor electrical power with subsequent reactor trip. To provide for this flow, each reactor coolant pump, regardless of design variation, shall contain a high-density flywheel and high-inertia motor. entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: PS-8002-0029, Revision 0.0

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Oil lift system pressure

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Vibration monitoring instruments for motor and pump shaft axial and radial displacement and vibrations

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Pump performance monitoring instrumentation provided by the Supplier, with the exception of instrumentation necessary to ensure coastdown upon pump trip at full plant power, is not considered nuclear safety-related.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: For non-safety related functions, one instrument is generally sufficient. Redundant instrumentation should be used when failure of the instrument would cause an unacceptable response, such as plant shutdown or system transit.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: If redundant instruments are used, the following guidelines shall be applied:

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Three instruments shall be used for instruments that are used in critical control functions, or that need to have their failures identified and addressed immediately. The control system will utilize signal selection logic to automatically identify and discard an instrument that diverges from the other two without impacting any system function.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Two instruments may be used if the instrument is not used in a control function and operators can identify a failed channel when the two channels diverge. Identification of the failed channel is typically inferred from a secondary measurement. Upon channel divergence, the system will lock in the last known good value until the operator can identify the failed channel.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The following instrumentation will be provided by the Buyer:

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Voltage and current sensors (ammeters) to monitor motor load and electrical input.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Pump Assembly Supports

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: RCP pump supports shall be designed in accordance with ASME Section III Division 1, Subsection NF (Supports), 2021 Edition as supplemented by API 610 (12th Edition). The vertical and horizontal support connections for the hydraulic section shall be integrally forged (or cast with prior Buyer approval) with the pump casing. Additional restraints and dampers as needed for the motor section shall be included in the overall pump assembly design.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The Supplier's pump assembly design shall allow for the support attachment points at the top and bottom to be repositioned by the Buyer, i.e., rotated about the axis of the pump, to allow for the best spacing availability below and directly adjacent to the pumps within the pumps' containment location envelopes.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: PS-8002-0029, Revision 0.0

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The upper horizontal support element (collar) for each RCP's lateral supports (snubbers) shall be located on the pumps such that the snubbers can be connected from the collar to the adjacent concrete slab at plant elevation (El.) -22'-0" (refer to Appendix B).

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: To ensure structural integrity and stability, the composite pump assembly support structure must be robust enough to bear the weight of the pump, motor, and any associated components, as well as dynamic forces during operation. Specific load combinations that need to be considered include dead loads, live loads, thermal loads, seismic loads, and dynamic loads due to pump operation.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The design of pump supports must ensure structural integrity under normal, upset, emergency, and faulted conditions.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump supporting structure shall permit the entire pump assembly to endure the SSE loads specified in Section 14.8 of this Specification.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Proper alignment between the pump and motor is crucial to prevent excessive wear and tear on the bearings and other components. Pump supports shall allow for the needed adjustments by the Buyer to maintain precise alignment and leveling. The support attachment points must ultimately allow for free (equal) thermal movements between the RPV nozzles and the RCP nozzles.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Materials used for the support structure shall be resistant to corrosion or otherwise be coated per Section 14.10 of this Specification, due to the harsh environmental conditions and corrosiveness of the pumped fluid. Consideration shall be given to the thermal expansion and contraction of materials used in the pump and support structure, and any of their coatings, due to the range of ambient and fluid temperatures.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The supporting structure shall prevent excessive vibrations, which can lead to mechanical failures, noise, and reduced pump life. The support structure shall be designed to absorb or isolate vibrations generated during pump operation. To minimize vibration transmission to the foundation and/or surrounding structures, vibration isolators or dampeners shall be included in the supporting design as needed.

Pump nozzle loads must be evaluated under various load combinations as specified in ASME Section III, NB-3200 (Design by Analysis) and NB-3600 (Piping Design). These combinations include dead loads, pressure loads, thermal loads, seismic loads, and other dynamic effects.

The Supplier shall provide the pump nozzle loads and load combinations to the Buyer to allow the Buyer to analyze and properly design the connected RCS piping and piping supports. The Buyer will notify the Supplier if the final piping design results in increased loads on the pump nozzles.

1. Design, procurement, and manufacturing records for nuclear safety-related components must be retained by the Supplier for the entire operational lifetime of the nuclear plant and of each component.
2. Non-safety-related documentation shall be maintained by the Supplier for a minimum of 10 years.

The Holtec SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps (RCPs) are major components of the plant's Reactor Coolant System (RCS). The RCS consists of the Reactor Pressure Vessel (RPV), a single once-through Steam Generator (SG) with an integrally connected Pressurizer, and two RCPs. Each pump is located in an individual cold leg between the SG and RPV. There will be two separate hot legs between the RPV and SG. Refer to Figure 12-1 below for a simplified flow diagram (the hot legs are shown in red, and the cold legs are shown in blue). Refer to Appendix A for a conceptual RCS equipment layout drawing. Refer to Appendix B for draft equipment layout within the SMR-300 containment.
Figure 12-1 Simplified Holtec SMR-300 RCS

The cold legs will be constructed from SA-106 Gr. C carbon steel piping having a 24" inside diameter, 30" outside diameter, 2.75" wall thickness, and a 0.250" thick SA-312 TP304 stainless-steel interior cladding. Cold leg design pressure and temperature are 2,485 psig and 650 °F, respectively. At 100% reactor power, normal operating pressure (NOP) and normal operating temperature (NOT) in the RCS cold legs are 2,250 psia and approximately 546 °F, respectively.

The reactor coolant consists of demineralized water containing a maximum of 2,500 ppm to 2,600 ppm of boric acid at beginning of core life (BOL). During cold conditions at this concentration, the added boric acid does not appreciably affect the specific gravity (SG) of the demineralized water, i.e., the specific gravity remains at approximately 1.0. entries.text: PS-8002-0029, Revision 0.0

To ensure stable pumping over the entire range of operation, the characteristics of each pump should be such that an increase in head always produces a decrease in flow, i.e., rising head-capacity characteristic. The head-flow characteristic curves for pumps used in parallel operation should constantly rise toward shutoff, and these curves should also be similar enough to assure that the pumps will operate at the same point and divide the load evenly. The two RCS piping cold legs (refer to Appendix A) will essentially consist of the exact same configuration and it is thus required that the two pumps operate uniformly and in concert. It is expected that two pumps operating in parallel will operate at the same head but at double the flow rate of an individual pump.

The seismic stresses on the pump section shall be treated as a primary stress as defined and limited per ASME Section III. The effects of seismic loading on the pump must be superimposed on stresses from all other expected sources in the required ASME Section III stress analysis, and this also includes the pump support attachments.

entries.section_title: Finite Element Modeling of Complete Pump Assemblies
entries.text: The Supplier is required to model the complete pump assembly as a "super element" using ANSYS software. The model must accurately represent the pump's physical, mechanical, and dynamic characteristics for use in finite element analysis (FEA) of the overall system in which the pump will be integrated.

entries.section_title: Finite Element Modeling of Complete Pump Assemblies
entries.text: The Supplier shall contact the Buyer's Technical Contact to request any information necessary to complete an accurate model.
Software: ANSYS (latest version compatible with ANSYS Workbench and Mechanical APDL).
Element Type: Super element (substructure) representation.
Degrees of Freedom: Include all relevant degrees of freedom to capture the pump assembly's dynamic behavior.
Material Properties: Accurate material properties, including density, Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, and damping coefficients.
Boundary Conditions: Appropriate boundary conditions reflecting the operational environment.
Ensure the super element model accurately represents the pump’s physical behavior.
Cross-check against detailed FEA models or experimental data.
Perform test simulations to verify the super element’s performance under different loading and boundary conditions.
ANSYS project file containing the super element model of the pump. Detailed documentation explaining the modeling process, assumptions, and validation results.

A comprehensive report detailing the dynamic characteristics of the pump assembly, including natural frequencies, mode shapes, and response to operational loads. Comparison of super element results with full detailed model or empirical data for validation purposes.
A user guide for integrating the super element model into larger system models, including instructions for setting up boundary conditions and applying loads.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The type of RCPs to be procured is a vertical motor-driven single stage centrifugal shaft-sealed pump assembly with bottom suction and radial discharge having a controlled or limited leakage pump shaft sealing system, as further described below.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The main components of shaft-sealed pumps are the pump case assembly, the pump cover and heat exchanger assembly, the driver mount, the rotating element assembly (shaft, impeller, and couplings) and the shaft seal assembly. The pump driver consists of a squirrel-cage AC induction type motor. The shaft seal assembly is to include a small coil-type heat exchanger, a shaft mounted auxiliary impeller, multiple mechanical seals, and seal pressure breakdown devices. The seal assembly functions to minimize the leakage of reactor coolant past the shaft and into the containment structure (CS). A flywheel is to be installed on the motor rotor to increase pump coast down time after a loss of electrical power with the plant at full power. The shaft-sealed RCPs are to be mounted vertically with the motor on top of the pump assembly with the casing on the bottom welded to the RCS cold leg piping.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump assemblies to be provided under this project shall comply with all the detailed requirements of this Specification. The selected Supplier will ultimately be responsible for the overall design, procurement of materials, fabrication, testing, cleaning, packaging, and shipping of the complete pump assemblies, including any specialized tooling and necessary spare parts.

entries.text: The reactor coolant pump shall be designed such that seal replacement can be achieved without draining down the reactor coolant system and shall minimize the time and effort required in the containment to remove and replace a pump shaft seal. This shall include design features such as improved access for lifting and handling, permanent services at the pumps, special handling equipment and tooling for the seal and coupling parts, and service and instrument connections which can be rapidly connected and disconnected or left in place. It shall be an objective to complete the seal replacement activity in containment within a maximum time limit of two 10-hour shifts.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Instrumentation shall be provided so that the plant operators can confirm the normal operation of the shaft seal assembly, detect and characterize seal degradation or failure, and monitor operation with degraded or failed stages. Pumps are to be provided with instrumentation sufficient to adequately monitor the sealing system over their anticipated ranges for normal operation (including startups and shutdowns), anticipated operational occurrences, and accident conditions. The provided instrumentation shall be in accordance with Section 14.2.17 of this Specification.

entries.section_title: 14.2.9 Pump Hydraulic Bearings and Lubrication Oil System
entries.text: The pump's rotating element shall be supported horizontally by radial type bearings. The rotating element's dead weight and hydraulic thrust shall be absorbed by thrust type bearings.

entries.section_title: 14.2.9 Pump Hydraulic Bearings and Lubrication Oil System
entries.text: All pump bearings shall provide adequate stiffness to control shaft motion, protect the pump impeller and shaft labyrinths from wear, and avoid contact between the motor stator and rotor. RCP bearings are to provide long life with negligible wear. The bearing loads are to be maintained within component load capabilities even under the severe conditions experienced during seismic events. The bearing/shaft design and loadings are to be established by analysis and testing.

entries.section_title: 14.2.9 Pump Hydraulic Bearings and Lubrication Oil System
entries.text: The pump bearing oil system shall provide the means to lift the pump motor rotor off the thrust bearing to reduce RCP starting current and to allow hand rotation of the rotor to facilitate alignment. An acceptable means of meeting this requirement is a hydraulic oil lift system. An oil lift pump configured for a 480VAC power supply may be mounted externally on the side of the pump housing. The lift system should include a pressure and time permissive (with defeats) prior to starting the RCP.

entries.section_title: 14.2.9 Pump Hydraulic Bearings and Lubrication Oil System
entries.text: The bearing oil system shall be designed in accordance with 10CFR50 Appendix A General Design Criterion (GDC) #3, and USNRC Regulatory Guide 1.189 Revision 5. Overall system design shall not result in posing a fire hazard within the reactor containment structure. The pump lube oil cooler piping system must be designed in accordance with ASME B31.1-2022 and be able to withstand the site safe shutdown earthquake (SSE) loads without oil leakage and without causing an oil fire.

entries.text: The pump motors shall be provided with the capability to install radial, non-contacting, proximity probes in at least the following locations:
i. Pump-to-motor coupling; and
ii. Two different axial locations in the motor.

Instrumentation which provides a once-per-revolution signal shall also be provided. These proximity probes and their leads should be arranged so that they need not be removed to perform routine pump maintenance, e.g., seal removal and replacement and alignment of the motor and pump. Where that is not practical, the design shall facilitate probe or cable handling including calibration and gapping of the probes.

The motor shall be equipped with six (6) nickel, ungrounded, resistance-type temperature detectors (120 ohms at 0°C) provided in the windings of the motor. Other materials may be acceptable with prior Buyer approval; however, the use of aluminum is not acceptable in this application. A suitable connection box, separate from the connection box for the motor leads shall be furnished for the temperature detector lead terminals.
The motor shall be equipped with grounding pads.

As applicable to the motor type, strip heaters are to be incorporated to prevent condensation from forming in the motor during extended idle periods. Connections shall be suitable to a 480VAC power supply when the heaters are required to be placed into service. The Supplier shall determine the number, type, and total power output of the heating system as well as the recommended ambient conditions when such heating is required. All such relevant information is to be included on the motor design drawings and related documentation.

Suitable lifting fixtures shall be provided on the pump motor to facilitate handling. Due to the substantial motor weights and their physical locations within the Containment Structure directly near other nuclear safety-related equipment, the following regulatory requirements are required to be incorporated when designing motor lifting appurtenances:
i. NUREG-0612, Control of Heavy Loads at Nuclear Power Plants (1980)
ii. NUREG-0554, Single-Failure-Proof Cranes for Nuclear Power Plants (1979)

Means of accurately achieving and verifying motor shaft to pump shaft alignment shall be provided. The required alignment procedure shall not require loosening of the pump closure studs. Means shall be provided to adjust the balance of the motor/pump rotor assembly at the coupling between the motor and the pump shaft.

Design provisions to allow "barring over" the pump and motor are desired. This refers to provisions to permit hand turning of the rotor assembly using simple tools, such as a bar, to ensure the rotor is unbound and moves freely prior to starting. The preferred location of such provisions is on top of the motor.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Within each Holtec SMR-300 unit, the two RCPs will circulate reactor coolant through the nuclear core at a total rate of approximately 12,000 lbm/sec (~121,100 gpm) or 6,000 lbm/sec (~60,550 gpm) per pump. This total flow rate provides heat removal for the 1,050 MWth thermal rating of the core. The pumps are to be driven by a squirrel cage induction motor powered from the plant's 4,160V non-vital (i.e., non-safety related) AC distribution system. Both pumps must be running during plant power operations.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The Holtec SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps shall be based on similar designs found in traditional as well as advanced operating PWRs. The following selected major design provisions are required:

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: A controlled or limited leakage pump shaft sealing system to minimize external leakage from the pump into the containment, including during a station black-out (SBO) event.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: A flywheel to extend flow coast down after a loss of pump electrical power to maintain flow through the core thereby improving the margin to departure from nucleate boiling (DNB).

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: An anti-reverse rotation device to prevent the pump from turning backwards which would increase core bypass flow and pump starting current.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The overall SMR-300 plant design life is 80 years. The expected design life of the pump casings and impellers is 80 years, which is the plant design life. The design life of the motor is expected to be 40 years, minimum. The RCP seal package operating life desired is 48 months, minimum. The Supplier is to address part obsolescence during the plant design life to achieve the 80 years of service required, including specifying the required preventive maintenance and part replacement schedules.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The Supplier's safety classification of individual pump assembly parts and subcomponents shall be established to ensure the pump assemblies are fully capable of performing the above specified safety-related functions for the duration of the design component/plant life.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: 14.1 RCP Design Code and Design Parameters

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: The SMR-300 RCPs shall be designed, fabricated, inspected, and tested in full compliance with the 2021 edition of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Code Section III, Division 1, Subsection NB for Class 1 components.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Each pump shall meet the following requirements:

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Service Levels: The pump shall be capable of sustaining operational loads and stresses corresponding to Service Levels A (Normal), B (Upset), C (Emergency), and D (Faulted).

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Stress Evaluation: Stress limits for the overall pump assembly (i.e., casing and nozzles) shall comply with Subsection NB for all postulated conditions thereby ensuring an adequate safety margin against all primary, secondary, and peak stresses. Fatigue evaluations must confirm cyclic load resistance.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Material Requirements: Materials shall meet NB-2000 specifications, including certification and traceability requirements.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Design Criteria: The pump design shall conform to NB-3400 (Pump Design), NB-3500 (Valve Design), and NB-3600 (Piping Design), as applicable. Supports and connections must meet Subsection NF (2021 Edition).

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Seismic and Accident Conditions: The pump shall withstand seismic loads and other dynamic forces without functional failure under Service Level D conditions.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Fabrication and Quality Assurance: Fabrication, installation, examination, and testing shall adhere to NB-4000, NB-5000, and NB-6000 to ensure the integrity of all pressure boundaries and welds.

entries.section_title: 14.0 REACTOR COOLANT PUMP SPECIFIC DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
entries.text: Documentation and Certification: All documentation, including certified material test reports (CMTRs), design calculations, and inspection records, shall comply with Subsection NB requirements for Class 1 components.

entries.text: The pump assemblies will be placed in the SMR-300 site warehouse for long-term storage after receipt.
Any special rigging requirements or instructions applicable to the pump assemblies while in their shipping containers shall be provided to the Buyer.

The pump assemblies shall be packaged assuming long-term site storage. All motor leads and other motor entrances to internal wiring shall be effectively protected or sealed, to prevent entrance of moisture, dust, and dirt. All openings into items shall be capped, plugged, and sealed. Weld end preparations shall be protected from corrosion and physical damage. Items subject to detrimental corrosion, either internal or external, shall be suitably protected. Items shall be blocked, braced and/or cushioned as appropriate for the shipping method to prevent physical damage. It shall be assured that the blocking, bracing, or cushioning items themselves do not cause physical damage during shipment and long-term storage.
All documentation (reports, drawings, etc.) shall include the following minimum required information:
Purchase Order Number
Holtec Project Number: 8002
Equipment Identification (Tag) Numbers - refer to Appendix D
All Technical Reports shall include a Table of Contents.
All documentation is to be provided in native and electronic PDF format.
All documentation shall be sent to the Buyer's Technical Contact as prescribed in Section 8.0 of this Specification.

For major documentation deliverables, the Supplier shall strive to submit in-progress drafts to the Buyer's Technical Contact at interim stages to permit early engagement and alignment with the Buyer's technical review team.
The Supplier should allow for the assumption of a review and comment cycle for each submittal having a 3-week duration.
Design documents, as applicable, shall include the required physical access envelope (clearances) needed for anticipated pump repair / replacement activities and normal operations and maintenance.

The pump design shall permit the loss and restoration of component cooling water while the pump is idle (cold legs) with all auxiliary systems in service (i.e., seal injection, component cooling water, etc.). A pump sitting idle at NOP/NOT shall not result in temperature gradients of pump components that would adversely impact pump starting and hydraulic performance.

Each pump assembly must be capable of standing idle in a partially filled system without requiring any special hydraulic procedures to prevent any adverse conditions that could cause malfunction. As applicable to the motor type, motors shall be equipped with strip heaters per Section 14.3 of this Specification to prevent condensation during extended lay-up periods.

This Purchase Specification provides the technical, documentation, and quality assurance requirements for the design, manufacture, testing, and shipment of complete Reactor Coolant Pump (RCP) assemblies for Holtec’s SMR-300 advanced nuclear power electrical generation station. "Pump assemblies" in this document refers to the entire manufactured component, i.e., the hydraulic pump section joined with the motor section.

SMR, LLC, based in Camden, NJ, is a wholly owned subsidiary of Holtec International and is the owner and designer of the two-unit SMR-300 plant site planned to be constructed at the existing Palisades nuclear plant site in Covert, Michigan where the RCP assemblies are to be installed.

This document supplements the formal Purchase Order (PO) between the selected Supplier (KSB) and Holtec International ("Buyer") and has been prepared in accordance with Holtec procedure HSP-100402, "Purchase Specifications", Revision 4.

The Supplier shall furnish Reactor Coolant pumps and motors, spare parts and tooling in the quantities and per the schedule delineated in the Purchase Order, in accordance with all agreed upon Terms and Conditions attached to the Purchase Order. The pump assemblies shall be complete with all associated supporting systems and instrumentation defined herein.

The Supplier shall be responsible for design, engineering, manufacturing, including supply, and assembly of equipment, the supply of drawings and data, all sub-Supplier coordination, inspection, testing, cleaning, packaging, and shipping of each pump assembly and all items included in the scope of this equipment specification. The Supplier shall deliver all equipment to the Buyer in accordance with the agreed upon delivery schedule.

The Holtec SMR-300 is a small modular reactor (SMR) nuclear electrical generating station with an output of approximately 300 MW electrical (MWe) per unit. It is an advanced pressurized water reactor (PWR) plant based on existing light water reactor (LWR) technologies consisting of two reactor coolant loops with a common steam generator. Each reactor coolant loop will contain one RCP. The SMR-300 station for which the RCPs are to be provided will consist of two units which will be constructed and located in Covert, Michigan at the same site as the existing Palisades Nuclear Plant. The station will be licensed under current US NRC regulations codified principally in Title 10 CFR Part 50.

The output of each of the two reactor cores is approximately 1,050 MW thermal (MWt). The units are designed for a nominal 18-month refueling cycle with flexibility for longer or shorter cycles depending upon the operating utility’s requirements. The overall plant design life is 80 years.

The following are the minimum requirements for the cleaning, packaging, and shipment of the competed pump assemblies. The intent of the following requirements is to ensure protection against corrosion, contamination, physical damage, or any effect which would lower the quality or cause the pump assemblies to deteriorate during the entire time the items are being shipped, handled, and stored.
Cleaning and cleanliness control of the completed pump assemblies shall be in accordance with Subpart 2.1 of ASME NQA-1 for Class B.

Items, just before packaging, shall have been inspected for cleanliness. Dirt, oil residue, metal chips or other forms of contamination shall have been removed by approved cleaning methods. Any entrapped water shall have been removed.
Packaging and shipment of the completed pump assemblies shall be in accordance with Subpart 2.2 of ASME NQA-1 for Level B. The following criteria shall also apply:
The pump assemblies shall be packaged assuming long-term site storage.
All motor leads and other motor entrances to internal wiring shall be effectively protected or sealed, to prevent entrance of moisture, dust, and dirt.
All openings into items shall be capped, plugged, and sealed. Weld end preparations shall be protected from corrosion and physical damage.
Items subject to detrimental corrosion, either internal or external, shall be suitably protected.

Items shall be blocked, braced and/or cushioned as appropriate for the shipping method to prevent physical damage. It shall be assured that the blocking, bracing, or cushioning items themselves do not cause physical damage during shipment and long-term storage.

Since the flywheel is involved in reactor protection analysis, it is nuclear safety-related and is subject to periodic regulatory required integrity inspections, and thus must be designed to easily permit such inspections. 10CFR Part 21 for the reporting of defects and non-compliance applies to the flywheel.

Each reactor coolant pump shall have the coast down characteristics specified in Appendix D which assure adequate RCS flow during pump coast down after interruption of power to the pump motor. This ensures thermal margins in the core following pump trip.

Adequate rotational inertia shall be provided by the pump-motor assembly itself, preferably without special internal configurations which add inertia. Permanently connected rotating machinery shall not be used to effectively increase the inertia and decrease the rate of coast down. That is, the use of either external flywheels or electrically connected rotating machinery is prohibited, since extra rotating equipment and electrical connections will add complexity to the plant and will add to the in-service inspection and maintenance burdens.

The determination of required rotational inertia shall account for operation of the pumps with dips in grid frequency. Pumps shall be designed to continue operation under off normal frequency conditions. It is possible for the voltage at the terminals of the pumps to vary from 100% to 85% of rated. For the Palisades SMR-300 site, the design shall be for a frequency range of 57.6 Hz to 61.2 Hz @ 85% rated voltage. On a loss of all VAC power, Appendix D identifies a coastdown requirement of 30% flow @ 30 seconds. Pump motors should be capable of indefinite operation at 85% voltage and @ 57.6 Hz.
Compliance with the following requirements shall apply to the pump assembly flywheel(s):
2. 10CFR50 Appendix A General Design Criteria 1 and 4
3. NRC Regulatory Guide 1.14 Rev. 1
4. NRC Standard Review Plan (NUREG-0800 Rev. 3) Section 5.4.1.1

Pump assembly design shall be such where the flywheel is enclosed wholly within the pump motors. The use of flywheels external to the pump or motor assemblies or located within the pump casing themselves (internal) is prohibited.
Mechanical stresses on the entire pump assembly during pump start-ups shall be considered in the determination of the final flywheel size, material, mass, and moments of inertia.

The Supplier shall analyze and document that in the event of a flywheel failure, the surrounding motor housing components are adequate to prevent missiles from jeopardizing the structural integrity of the reactor coolant system and other plant structures, systems and components. The analysis shall provide certification that the RCP flywheel and motor housing were analyzed to demonstrate that a fractured flywheel cannot potentially impair the operation of nearby safety-related systems or components.

The analysis of flywheel capture is to be predicated on energy calculations, presented as a fraction of the energy necessary to totally breach the motor housing. Each flywheel requires testing at an overspeed condition under both normal RCS cold and hot conditions to verify the flywheel design and construction.

Additionally, if an internal flywheel is used in the RCP, the design and construction of the flywheel shall minimize areas of high stress concentration, provide suitable material toughness, and implement all the fabrication and examination procedures necessary to achieve a high level of integrity throughout the plant's operating life.

Access to the flywheel for maintenance will require pump and/or motor removal and disassembly, which would increase personnel radiation exposure and potentially impact plant availability. The flywheel should therefore be designed such that planned maintenance and inspection activities are not required beyond those already planned for the pump assembly itself. The Supplier shall show that the flywheel design is such that it does not add to the burden of pump maintenance and does not require periodic in-service inspection, other than that which may be regulatory required.

For a motor-mounted flywheel, overspeed testing with the motor uncoupled from the pump is acceptable. Testing of the flywheel at hot and cold RCS conditions would only be required for a flywheel located inside the pump casing which is exposed to RCS temperature conditions.

The design of the pump shall be such as to preclude the instantaneous stopping of any rotating component of the pump or motor. Due to the potential significant effect on the reactor core and RCS pressure due to RCP motor seizure (i.e., locked rotor) of one or both pumps while the plant is at power, the Supplier shall provide the failure mechanisms and the probability of the instantaneous complete stopping of any pump assembly rotating element with the plant at full power, i.e., RCPs at nominal full speed and RCS conditions at NOP/NOT. An instantaneous stop of the impeller is considered a conservative assumption that bounds any slower stop or coast down. This information will allow Holtec to perform a transient analysis to determine the effect of a locked rotor on the RCS pressure and RCS pressure which will be necessary to demonstrate that acceptable reactor core and boundary radiological consequence limits are not exceeded due to departure from nucleate boiling (DNB).
The stresses in the pump casing and motor housing are to be analyzed using the ASME B&PV Code, Section III, Service Level D limits for this condition.

entries.text: The Supplier shall ensure the pump’s required net positive suction head (NPSHr) is such that the Buyer can assure the design of the RCS tumble margin above the system’s available net positive suction head (NPSHa). This will provide operational integrity and minimize the potential for cavitation.

It should be noted that the Holtec SMR-300 does not require reactor coolant pump operation to achieve safe shut down, and minimum net positive suction head requirements are not required to provide safe operation of the Holtec SMR-300. However, the margin between the required net positive suction head (NPSHr) and available net positive suction head (NPSHa) shall be no less than 15% of NPSHa.

The RCPs are to be driven by direct on-line (DOL) start motors. A variable frequency drive (VFD) system, as well as a motor soft-start system, were considered but ultimately will not be used for the Palisades project [38].

Pumps must be able to be started at full line voltage. Motor design is to accommodate the following when started DOL: (1) high in-rush currents; (2) thermal and mechanical stresses on the motor core and windings; and (3) mechanical stresses on the pump-motor shaft line associated with acceleration of the flywheel to operating speed.
Refer to Section 14.3 for specific RCP motor requirements.

The pump rotating element (shaft assembly) shall consist of the following sub-components: a) Pump drive shaft (motor end) b) Pump shaft (impeller end) c) Pump drive shaft to pump shaft coupling d) Thrust and radial bearings (see Section 14.2.9) e) Pump impeller (see Section 14.2.10)

The pump shaft assembly is to be a split-type design divided into two sections: the pump drive shaft (motor end) and the pump shaft (impeller end) in order to permit servicing of the seal system without removing the motor or disassembling any bearings.

entries.text: Instrumentation shall be provided so that the plant operators can confirm the normal operation of the shaft seal assembly, detect and characterize seal degradation or failure, and monitor operation with degraded or failed stages. Pumps are to be provided with instrumentation sufficient to adequately monitor the sealing system over their anticipated ranges for normal operation (including startups and shutdowns), anticipated operational occurrences, and accident conditions. The provided instrumentation shall be in accordance with Section 14.2.17 of this Specification.

The pump's rotating element shall be supported horizontally by radial type bearings. The rotating element's dead weight and hydraulic thrust shall be absorbed by thrust type bearings. All pump bearings shall provide adequate stiffness to control shaft motion, protect the pump impeller and shaft labyrinths from wear, and avoid contact between the motor stator and rotor. RCP bearings are to provide long life with negligible wear. The bearing loads are to be maintained within component load capabilities even under the severe conditions experienced during seismic events. The bearing/shaft design and loadings are to be established by analysis and testing.

The pump bearing oil system shall provide the means to lift the pump motor rotor off the thrust bearing to reduce RCP starting current and to allow hand rotation of the rotor to facilitate alignment. An acceptable means of meeting this requirement is a hydraulic oil lift system. An oil lift pump configured for a 480VAC power supply may be mounted externally on the side of the pump housing. The lift system should include a pressure and time permissive (with defeats) prior to starting the RCP. The bearing oil system shall be designed in accordance with 10CFR50 Appendix A General Design Criterion (GDC) #3, and USNRC Regulatory Guide 1.189 Revision 5. Overall system design shall not result in posing a fire hazard within the reactor containment structure.

The pump lube oil cooler piping system must be designed in accordance with ASME B31.1-2022 and be able to withstand the site safe shutdown earthquake (SSE) loads without oil leakage and without causing an oil fire.

The pump casings constitute part of the RCS pressure boundary. They are designated as nuclear safety-related and must be designed and manufactured in accordance with ASME Section III Class 1 and 10CFR50 Appendix B. 10CFR Part 21 for the reporting of defects and noncompliance applies.

The pump casing can be loosely defined as that part of the pump structure which encases the impeller and diffuser and includes the suction and discharge nozzles. The casing serves two main purposes: 1. It is the primary pressure containment; and 2. It gives proper direction to the flow as the fluid passes through the pump.

The suction nozzle directs fluid to the impeller inlet. The impeller discharge is collected, diffused, and directed to the discharge nozzle by the casing. The Holtec SMR-300 RCP casings are to be the diffuser type.

The RCP casings will be butt-welded to 24" ID, 30" OD, 2.75" wall thickness SA-106 Gr. C carbon steel RCS piping having a 0.250" thick SA-312 TP304 stainless-steel ID cladding. Refer to Section 14.2.20 of this Specification for further information on welding the pump casings to the RCS piping.

Pump casing, impeller, and diffuser materials may be castings or forgings and shall utilize the following ASME Section II materials: 1) Casting (stainless-steel): SA-351, Gr. CF8M 2) Casting (carbon steel): SA-216, Gr. WCB 3) Forging (stainless-steel): SA-182, Gr. F316 or F6NM 4) Forging (carbon steel): SA-105, SA-266 Gr. The integrity of the reactor coolant pressure boundary.
The capability to shut down the reactor and maintain it in a safe shutdown condition.
The capability to prevent or mitigate the consequences of accidents that could release radiation to the public.
Refers to Holtec International as defined in [1] above.

The Engineer appointed by the Buyer to act as Engineer from time to time for the purpose of furnishing engineering as well as design and construction supervision services to the Owner/Purchaser in connection with the project in question. In the absence of such an appointment, the Client/Owner will be considered as engineer.

A formal acceptance process performed in accordance with ASME NQA-1 Subpart 2.14 to provide reasonable assurance that a commercial grade item or service will perform its intended nuclear safety-related function(s) via the verification of the item's or service's critical characteristics.

Non-safety-related components that are designed and installed using readily available industrial or commercial-grade parts and equipment without imposition of any additional quality assurance requirements. Commercial grade items may be upgraded to safety-related quality standards under a formal dedication process.

An item or service satisfying all three of the following criteria: 1) Not subject to design or specification requirements that are unique to nuclear facilities; 2) Used in applications other than nuclear facilities; 3) Is to be ordered from the manufacturer/supplier on the basis of specifications set forth in the manufacturer's/supplier's published product description (i.e., catalog).

Those important design, material, and performance characteristics of a commercial grade item that, once verified, will provide reasonable assurance that the item will perform its intended safety function.
The critical speed of a vertical centrifugal pump shaft is the speed at which the shaft's natural frequency matches the rotational speed, causing resonance.
Any deviation from a regulatory requirement, design basis, or manufacturing process that could result in a substantial safety hazard.
A postulated accident that a nuclear facility must be designed and built to withstand without loss to the systems, structures, and components necessary to ensure public health and safety.

entries.text: A potential plant unit accident in which a breach in a reactor's pressure boundary causes the coolant water to rush out of the reactor faster than makeup water can be added back in. Without sufficient coolant, the reactor core could heat up and potentially melt the zirconium fuel cladding, causing a major release of radioactivity.

SSCs required to ensure the safe operation of the plant, the prevention of accidents, or the mitigation of their consequences. These systems are primarily focused on supporting the operational efficiency and convenience of the plant but do not directly affect nuclear safety in the event of an accident or emergency. Non-safety-related components are typically designed and installed using commercial-grade parts and equipment.
The period during which an electrical generating unit or its transmission line is out of service. Outages may be forced or scheduled, and full or partial.

The maximum vibratory ground motion for which certain structures, systems, and components must be designed pursuant to Appendix S to 10CFR Part 50 to remain functional. This earthquake is based upon an evaluation of the maximum earthquake potential considering the regional and local geology and seismology and specific characteristics of local subsurface material. These structures, systems, and components are those necessary to ensure the following:

Refers to systems, structures, and components that are directly required to ensure the safe shutdown of the reactor, prevent or mitigate accidents, and maintain containment of radioactive materials. They are relied upon to remain functional during and following design-basis events. Their functionality ensures that key regulatory criteria, such as levels of radioactivity released, are met.

A coating system used in areas inside the reactor containment structure where coating failure could adversely affect the operation of post-accident fluid systems and thereby impair safe reactor shutdown. The coating is designed to withstand design basis incidents within the reactor containment structure without flaking or degrading.

Part of factory acceptance testing for a pump/motor assembly. The testing is designed to simulate the real-world operating conditions of the system over an extended period, ensuring that both the pump and motor can reliably perform as expected under normal and varying loads. This test evaluates the durability, performance, and efficiency of the assembly, focusing on its long-term operational reliability.

A formal procedure conducted at the final installation location to confirm that the delivered system, equipment, or component has been properly installed, integrated, and functions as intended under actual operating conditions. SAT ensures that the system meets all specified requirements, adheres to regulatory and safety standards, and is ready for commissioning or full operation.

For the SMR-300, the SBO event is defined as the complete loss of all offsite and onsite AC power for a period of 72 hours (3 days) without operator actions. The reactor will be in a safe shutdown condition with an average RCS temperature range of 420 °F ≤ Tavg > 200 °F during this time.
A condition that could significantly affect public health and safety or the environment.

The organization to which the Holtec Purchase Order is addressed which has the responsibility to provide the components and services specified herein in accordance with all Purchase Order and Purchase Specification technical, quality, and commercial requirements.

Any person or persons, or Purchaser (other than the Supplier) named by the Supplier in the Contract documents, or assigned afterwards to execute parts of Contract works after the written approval of Owner/Purchaser, including the legal personal representatives, successors, and assigns of such persons, who are accepted by the Owner/Supplier in writing.

Part of an NRC license authorizing the operation of a nuclear production facility. A Technical Specification establishes requirements for plant items such as safety limits, limiting safety system settings, limiting control settings, limiting conditions for operation, surveillance requirements, design features, and administrative controls.

It is neither the Purchaser’s intent to specify all technical requirements nor to set forth those requirements adequately covered by applicable latest codes and standards.

entries.text: The Holtec SMR-300 RCPs are necessary to provide sufficient flow during normal power operations to ensure adequate heat is transferred from the reactor core within the RPV to the Steam Generator via the reactor coolant water. The specific purposes of the RCPs are:
To provide the forced circulation of reactor coolant for the removal of core heat;
Maintain the departure from nucleate boiling ratio (DNBR) within the acceptable range during pump coast down after loss of all supplied reactor coolant pump motor electrical power; and
To provide energy to heat up the RCS from ambient temperature to greater than the minimum temperature required for criticality prior to reactor startup.
The Holtec SMR-300 RCPs have two safety-related functions:
The RCPs serve as part of the RCS pressure boundary for containing the reactor coolant; and
The RCPs maintain the minimum necessary reactor flow for a defined time while coasting down after a loss of off-site power (LOOP) event with reactor trip.

The two RCPs are an integral part of the reactor coolant pressure boundary. The pumps are required to be designed, fabricated, and tested to quality standards consistent with the requirements set forth in the ASME B&PV Code Section III Division 1 for Class 1 components (Subsection NB) 2021 Edition, 10CFR50 Appendix B, ASME NQA-1, 10CFR50.55a, and 10CFR50 Appendix A General Design Criteria (GDC).

It should be noted that 10CFR50 Appendix A provides design criteria for the RCP design organization (Holtec International). These requirements are extended to the RCP design organization (Supplier) by means of this Specification, although the Buyer retains ultimate design responsibility. The 10CFR50 Appendix A design criteria specifically applicable to the Reactor Coolant Pumps include: 1, 2, 3, 4, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 30, 31, and 32.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Within each Holtec SMR-300 unit, the two RCPs will circulate reactor coolant through the nuclear core at a total rate of approximately 12,000 lbm/sec (~121,100 gpm) or 6,000 lbm/sec (~60,550 gpm) per pump. This total flow rate provides heat removal for the 1,050 MWth thermal rating of the core. The pumps are to be driven by a squirrel cage induction motor powered from the plant's 4,160V non-vital (i.e., non-safety related) AC distribution system. Both pumps must be running during plant power operations.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The Holtec SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps shall be based on similar designs found in traditional as well as advanced operating PWRs. The following selected major design provisions are required:

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: A controlled or limited leakage pump shaft sealing system to minimize external leakage from the pump into the containment, including during a station black-out (SBO) event.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: A flywheel to extend flow coast down after a loss of pump electrical power to maintain flow through the core thereby improving the margin to departure from nucleate boiling (DNB).

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: An anti-reverse rotation device to prevent the pump from turning backwards which would increase core bypass flow and pump starting current.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The overall SMR-300 plant design life is 80 years. The expected design life of the pump casings and impellers is 80 years, which is the plant design life. The design life of the motor is expected to be 40 years, minimum. The RCP seal package operating life desired is 48 months, minimum. The Supplier is to address part obsolescence during the plant design life to achieve the 80 years of service required, including specifying the required preventive maintenance and part replacement schedules.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps

entries.text: Pump motor winding insulation shall be as specified in Appendix D.
15.0 PUMP ASSEMBLY TESTING
15.1 Pre-Delivery Performance (Factory Acceptance) Testing

Pumps that are considered by the Supplier to be "first-of-a-kind" (FOAK) shall be performance tested to establish that the design meets all functional requirements. This testing shall be performed prior to delivery and is subject to the Buyer's approval. If a Supplier's existing pump design with long-term, successful operating experience in existing LWRs will be provided for the Holtec SMR-300 RCPs, then first-of-a-kind testing may be limited in scope or eliminated. However, a detailed technical justification is expected, i.e., any changes in the provided Holtec SMR-300 pump design from the pre-existing design need to be individually evaluated to assure the operating experience remains applicable.

Each first-of-a-kind pump design or significantly modified pump design shall be performance tested during hot and cold conditions as well as when starting cold and moving up through temperatures and as different speeds, to establish that the design meets all functional requirements. In particular, this testing shall:
Include at least 500 hours of typical in-plant operation (e.g., at actual temperature, pressure, head, flow, and water chemistry).

Include transients and upsets of sufficient number and severity (within the practical limitations of full-scale testing facilities) to provide assurance that the design requirements will be met in actual service.

Include demonstration that the leakage through the seals under loss of all AC power will be limited as specified (this demonstration may be performed using a test fixture rather than a complete pump).
Include complete disassembly and inspection after test.

The specific required tests are divided into three general categories: RCP hydraulic performance, motor performance, and operation transient performance tests, consisting of no less than the following listed tests. Testing is to be conducted at the specified NOP/NOT conditions. These tests, in aggregate, constitute "factory acceptance testing" (FAT).

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: PS-8002-0029, Revision 0.0

Cold Performance Characteristics Testing. "Cold coolant" exists with no initial flow when the first RCP is started with the coolant having a specific gravity of approximately 1.0 and a temperature of 100 °F.
Hot Performance Characteristics Testing
Electrical Balance Testing
Heat Insulation Resistance Testing

Service Cycle Testing – to include: start/stop cycles, load variations, operating runs, temperature monitoring, vibration and noise testing, efficiency and performance tests, electrical and mechanical stress testing, leakage and seal integrity, shutdowns and stops.
Pressure Pulsation Measurement Testing
Reduced Voltage Hang Up Testing
Loss of Power Testing
Loss of External Cooling Water Testing
Operational / Endurance Testing
Reverse Rotation Operability Testing
Forward Restart of Reverse Rotating Testing
Net Positive Suction Head Testing
Coast Down Testing to Complete Stop – time required between natural frequency and operating speed.
Overspeed and Critical Speed Testing – Verification of ± 25% separation margin between natural frequency and operating speed.
Flow Induced Vibration Testing. Confirm that the assembly can operate within vibration limits set by industry standards (ISO 10816 and/or API-610).

If the Supplier is unable to test at NOP/NOT conditions, then the Supplier is to explain in detail the analytical methods for the reliable and accurate extrapolation of cold or low-speed test data to hot or high-speed conditions. The Supplier shall consider the use of the following analytical methods:

Modal Analysis Identifies the natural frequencies, mode shapes, and damping ratios of the pump and its components. This analysis helps in understanding how the pump structure vibrates at different frequencies and is crucial for avoiding resonance conditions.

Harmonic Analysis Assesses the pump’s response to sinusoidal loads at various frequencies. This is important for understanding how operational forces (such as those from rotating imbalances or fluid flow pulsations) might induce vibrations.

Transient Dynamic Analysis Evaluates the pump’s response to time-varying loads during start-up, shutdown, and coastdown. This analysis can predict how the pump will behave under sudden changes in conditions, which are critical for safety assessments.

entries.text: PS-8002-0029, Revision 0.0

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump motor is not classified as Class 1E. Environmental and seismic qualification of the motor per the requirements of 10CFR50.49, NRC Regulatory Guide 1.89, and IEEE Standards 323 and 344 are not required.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Motor rating shall be 4160V, 3-phase, 60 cycles per second (Hz) with a Service Factor (SF) of 1.15 (continuous). It is expected that the motor will be normally operated at the nameplate horsepower. It is desired that the motor be capable, when necessary, of an output of 1.15 times the rated horsepower during plant power operations (hot conditions) with the motor provided with nameplate voltage and frequency. The service factor shall not be credited during motor starting and shall only be used to account for occasional overloads under normal running conditions.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: With only 85%-rated voltage available, the pump motor shall be capable of starting the pump in reactor coolant having a 1.0 specific gravity (SG), i.e., cold conditions. It is assumed the pump curve will be developed by the Supplier using a SG of 1.0. Thus, when ensuring satisfactory performance when the motor has only a 85% of rated voltage available, pump performance should be evaluated for pumping fluid with a SG of 1.0.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The motor shall be suitable for "across-the-line" starting with sustained full line voltage.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: It is desired that the pump assemblies be operated at synchronous speeds, i.e., the motor's rotor will spin at the same speed as the stator's rotating magnetic field. The optimum number of motor poles is 6 and the nominal operating motor speed is to be 1,200 rpm to ensure the best overall performance. The selected normal operating speed shall provide for a long motor life with minimal motor maintenance. The pump, motor, and flywheel design maximum speed shall be 125% of the selected normal operating speed. The entire pump assembly shall be capable of operation without mechanical damage at speeds up to, and including, 125% of normal speed.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The temperature rise of the motor when operating with a reactor coolant temperature of 500°F or above shall be in accordance with ANSI/NEMA MG 1-2021. The maximum normal ambient temperature is specified in Appendix D.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The average and hot spot temperatures, considering the effects of extremes of ambient temperatures, cooling water flow and temperature, and power consumption, shall not exceed the temperatures for which the motor insulation has been proven stable in service.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The three (3) stator winding leads shall be brought out into a conduit box mounted on the side of the motor.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Positive means of preventing RCP motor oil leakage from posing a fire hazard within containment as well as from entering the RCP shaft seals shall be provided. Design provisions shall be in accordance with USNRC Regulatory Guide 1.189 Revision 5. The oil collection system should not require removal when removing or installing an RCP shaft seal.
The pump motors shall be provided with the capability to install radial, non-contacting, proximity probes in at least the following locations:
i. Pump-to-motor coupling; and
ii. Two different axial locations in the motor.

Instrumentation which provides a once-per-revolution signal shall also be provided. These proximity probes and their leads should be arranged so that they need not be removed to perform routine pump maintenance, e.g., seal removal and replacement and alignment of the motor and pump. Where that is not practical, the design shall facilitate probe or cable handling including calibration and gapping of the probes.

The motor shall be equipped with six (6) nickel, ungrounded, resistance-type temperature detectors (120 ohms at 0°C) provided in the windings of the motor. Other materials may be acceptable with prior Buyer approval; however, the use of aluminum is not acceptable in this application. A suitable connection box, separate from the connection box for the motor leads shall be furnished for the temperature detector lead terminals.
The motor shall be equipped with grounding pads.

As applicable to the motor type, strip heaters are to be incorporated to prevent condensation from forming in the motor during extended idle periods. Connections shall be suitable to a 480VAC power supply when the heaters are required to be placed into service. The Supplier shall determine the number, type, and total power output of the heating system as well as the recommended ambient conditions when such heating is required. All such relevant information is to be included on the motor design drawings and related documentation.

Suitable lifting fixtures shall be provided on the pump motor to facilitate handling. Due to the substantial motor weights and their physical locations within the Containment Structure directly near other nuclear safety-related equipment, the following regulatory requirements are required to be incorporated when designing motor lifting appurtenances:
i. NUREG-0612, Control of Heavy Loads at Nuclear Power Plants (1980)
ii. NUREG-0554, Single-Failure-Proof Cranes for Nuclear Power Plants (1979)

Means of accurately achieving and verifying motor shaft to pump shaft alignment shall be provided. The required alignment procedure shall not require loosening of the pump closure studs. Means shall be provided to adjust the balance of the motor/pump rotor assembly at the coupling between the motor and the pump shaft.

Design provisions to allow "barring over" the pump and motor are desired. This refers to provisions to permit hand turning of the rotor assembly using simple tools, such as a bar, to ensure the rotor is unbound and moves freely prior to starting. The preferred location of such provisions is on top of the motor.
