entries.text: 1. The RCP assembly spare parts list, based on the Supplier’s recommendations, shall be provided to the Buyer in sufficient detail to allow the future ordering of spare parts. The spare parts list shall include notation of the Quality classification of each part, i.e., nuclear safety-related or commercial grade.
2. The spare parts list shall be itemized into the following categories:
a. Pump (hydraulic) section
b. Mechanical seal system
f. Oil lubrication system
g. Spare parts for special tools

3. When authorized by a formal Purchase Order from the Buyer, the Supplier shall provide the recommended spare parts in the quantities listed on the Purchase Order and deliver all items per the purchase order’s schedule requirements.
4. All ordered parts shall be robustly packaged to prevent damage during transit. Parts packages shall include the following information, at a minimum:
a. Buyer’s Purchase Order Number
d. Quantity and unit of measure
e. Applicable pump or motor model number
f. Supplier’s drawing number and BOM item number
g. Applicable documentation, such as: certified material test reports (CMTRs) and Certificates of Conformance, etc.
h. Special storage information (as applicable) such as: shelf-life limitations, required storage environmental conditions, and in-storage maintenance requirements

Any special tools necessary for the maintenance, disassembly, and reassembly of the RCP pump assemblies shall be furnished by the Supplier in the quantities listed on the Purchase Order. These tools may include, but are not limited to, the following:
Rotating Device – Used to mount the impeller from one side and the sealing arrangement from the other side to the sealing cover.
Platform for Rotating Device – Enables the mounting of the impeller and sealing arrangement to the sealing cover (rolling platform around rotating device).
Radiation Shield for the Impeller – Lowers dose in the area during impeller removal.
Radiation Shield for the Pump Casing – Lowers dose in the area of the pump casing.
Mock Hydraulic Pretensioner – Needed to apply pretension for the seal cover studs.

Mounting Device – Needed to mount/dismount the plain bearing, feeding unit, seal stage #1, pre-mounted sealing cover, intermediate piece, and coupling part with mounted motor. This tool consists of the following sub-parts: winch, rails, traverse, sled, adapter, and holder piece.
All items shall be delivered per the purchase order's schedule requirements and shall be packaged in the same fashion as detailed above for spare parts.
Marking and Identification of Pump Assemblies
Each entire pump hydraulic assembly (as a single unit) shall be ASME N-stamped after it meets all Section III criteria for nuclear safety-related applications.

Pump subcomponents, such as impellers, casings, seals, bearings, and fasteners, do not require individual ASME stamps. However, all subcomponents must be traceable and be manufactured with code-approved materials allowing the entire pump to be certified as compliant and ASME-stamped by the pump manufacturer.

entries.text: Bolted joints and threaded fasteners should be used only where a clear need for them has been established. The use of a bolted joint should include consideration of not only the first cost but the subsequent maintenance effort, the risk of service problems, and the risk of collecting radioactive material which such joints can introduce. Where a bolted joint must be used to satisfy functional requirements, its adequacy should preferentially be achieved by a simple, rugged design which does not depend on high strength or unusual materials, precision parts, or specialized assembly and inspection methods.

Threaded fasteners should be locked under the following conditions: (1) where the threaded fasteners are subjected to alternating loads which are a significant fraction of their minimum pre-load and especially where the fastener's pre-load could be released by small deformations of the fastener or joint parts; or (2) where the threaded fastener cannot be pre-loaded significantly even though the expected loads are small.

A locking device shall: (1) not have any parts which vibrate excessively; (2) require a minimum of technician skill to disassemble and reassemble; and (3) allow for easy inspection and verification of proper installation without disassembly.

Fasteners shall be locked by a method which retains the broken fastener parts. Where failure of the load carrying portion of a single threaded fastener will result in a loose part which has a high probability of causing damage to other components which would result in serious personal injury or require extensive down time or high cost to repair, the locking means shall provide for the retention of the broken fastener parts as well as preventing rotation.

Bolted joints must be easily inspectable, located on the exterior of the pump assembly, and not be covered or obscured by other components (where possible) to allow for the required ASME B&PV Code Section XI Inservice Inspection (ISI) non-destructive examination (NDE) purposes.
RCP casing flange closures shall be designed so that: a) Leakage from the main closure gasket(s) can be detected; and
b) Leakage can be prevented from wetting (and corroding) closure bolting and other structural components and can be directed to a suitable collection point.
One potential acceptable method to meet these requirements is the use of double (i.e., two separate) flange gaskets with a means to monitor the space between the two gaskets.

The leakage detection method shall have enough sensitivity such that leakage can be detected before the represents a major operational problem; however, it shall not result in false leakage indications. The detection method shall allow for continuous monitoring and remote indication and alarming.

entries.section_title: Pump Design Provisions Due to Absence of RCS Vacuum Fill
entries.text: The Holtec SMR-300 plant will not be provided with provisions to vacuum fill the reactor coolant system after refueling outages. Use of a vacuum system for refilling the RCS after the system is drained for maintenance or refueling via the removal of air and non-condensable gases would, if utilized, reduce the time required for RCS fill and potentially reduce the wear and tear on the reactor coolant pumps. The RCPs shall be designed with suitable provisions, as deemed necessary by the Supplier, to prevent potential pump hydraulic damage over the plant lifetime as the result of pump startup with the RCS piping less than 100% full of coolant.

In the Holtec SMR-300 RCS, the two RCPs will be operated in parallel at 100% power, with one pump in each cold leg. The Supplier is required to consider and address problems associated with potential parallel pump operational configurations for both hot and cold coolant conditions including, but not limited to the following:
Only one of the two pumps running with reverse flow through the idle pump.
Flow imbalance between running pumps.
NPSH discharge flows significantly lower than the best efficiency point (BEP).

Motor current starting draw for the various parallel pump operational configurations must also be considered for both hot and cold conditions. Both pumps are expected to be operated at cold conditions during Mode 5 (Cold Shutdown) with a RCS average temperature of approximately 200 °F (or less) for 12 to 36 hours for chemical addition purposes (i.e., crude burst).

Each assembly (pump and motor) is to be provided with the following instrumentation, at a minimum. Instruments shall be local and allow for remote indications and alarms in the plant's main control room where warranted.
Resistance temperature detector (RTD) elements to monitor for high bearing water temperatures
Temperature detectors for motor stator winding, motor bearings, and radial and thrust bearings
Seal water temperatures, ΔP, and flows
Seal cavity leakage flows, pressures, and leak off temperatures
Temperature and flow rate for staging flow (hydrodynamic seal), seal injection, and seal injection pump cooling
Inlet and outlet fluid temperatures for the HP cooler
Motor cooling air temperature
Speed sensors to monitor motor speed (rpm's)
Oil level and oil temperature for pump thrust bearings
Oil level for leakage collection

entries.text: Pump performance monitoring instrumentation provided by the Supplier, with the exception of instrumentation necessary to ensure coastdown upon pump trip at full plant power, is not considered nuclear safety-related.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: For non-safety related functions, one instrument is generally sufficient. Redundant instrumentation should be used when failure of the instrument would cause an unacceptable response, such as plant shutdown or system transit.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: If redundant instruments are used, the following guidelines shall be applied:

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Three instruments shall be used for instruments that are used in critical control functions, or that need to have their failures identified and addressed immediately. The control system will utilize signal selection logic to automatically identify and discard an instrument that diverges from the other two without impacting any system function.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Two instruments may be used if the instrument is not used in a control function and operators can identify a failed channel when the two channels diverge. Identification of the failed channel is typically inferred from a secondary measurement. Upon channel divergence, the system will lock in the last known good value until the operator can identify the failed channel.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The following instrumentation will be provided by the Buyer:

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Voltage and current sensors (ammeters) to monitor motor load and electrical input.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: RCP pump supports shall be designed in accordance with ASME Section III Division 1, Subsection NF (Supports), 2021 Edition as supplemented by API 610 (12th Edition). The vertical and horizontal support connections for the hydraulic section shall be integrally forged (or cast with prior Buyer approval) with the pump casing. Additional restraints and dampers as needed for the motor section shall be included in the overall pump assembly design.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The Supplier's pump assembly design shall allow for the support attachment points at the top and bottom to be repositioned by the Buyer, i.e., rotated about the axis of the pump, to allow for the best spacing availability below and directly adjacent to the pumps within the pumps' containment location envelopes.

entries.text: Suitable lifting fixtures shall be provided on the pump motor to facilitate handling. Due to the substantial motor weights and their physical locations within the Containment Structure directly near other nuclear safety-related equipment, the following regulatory requirements are required to be incorporated when designing motor lifting appurtenances:
NUREG-0612, Control of Heavy Loads at Nuclear Power Plants (1980)
NUREG-0554, Single-Failure-Proof Cranes for Nuclear Power Plants (1979)
Means of accurately achieving and verifying motor shaft to pump shaft alignment shall be provided. The required alignment procedure shall not require loosening of the pump closure studs.
Means shall be provided to adjust the balance of the motor/pump rotor assembly at the coupling between the motor and the pump shaft.

Design provisions to allow "barring over" the pump and motor are desired. This refers to provisions to permit hand turning of the rotor assembly using simple tools, such as a bar, to ensure the rotor is unbound and moves freely prior to starting. The preferred location of such provisions is on top of the motor.

entries.text: Proper alignment between the pump and motor is crucial to prevent excessive wear and tear on the bearings and other components. Pump supports shall allow for the needed adjustments by the Buyer to maintain precise alignment and leveling. The support attachment points must ultimately allow for free (equal) thermal movements between the RPV nozzles and the RCP nozzles. Materials used for the support structure shall be resistant to corrosion or otherwise be coated per Section 14.10 of this Specification, due to the harsh environmental conditions and corrosiveness of the pumped fluid. Consideration shall be given to the thermal expansion and contraction of materials used in the pump and support structure, and any of their coatings, due to the range of ambient and fluid temperatures. The supporting structure shall prevent excessive vibrations, which can lead to mechanical failures, noise, and reduced pump life. The support structure shall be designed to absorb or isolate vibrations generated during pump operation. To minimize vibration transmission to the foundation and/or surrounding structures, vibration isolators or dampeners shall be included in the supporting design as needed.

Pump nozzle loads must be evaluated under various load combinations as specified in ASME Section III, NB-3200 (Design by Analysis) and NB-3600 (Piping Design). These combinations include dead loads, pressure loads, thermal loads, seismic loads, and other dynamic effects. The Supplier shall provide the pump nozzle loads and load combinations to the Buyer to allow the Buyer to analyze and properly design the connected RCS piping and piping supports. The Buyer will notify the Supplier if the final piping design results in increased loads on the pump nozzles.

entries.section_title: Welding of Pump Casing Nozzles to RCS Piping
entries.text: For non-Code welding, all weld procedures and welders shall be qualified in accordance with ASME Section IX (2021).

entries.section_title: Welding of Pump Casing Nozzles to RCS Piping
entries.text: The two pump casing nozzles will be butt-welded to the RCS piping by the Buyer during plant construction. Current SMR-300 plant RCS design provides for the cold legs to be constructed from SA-106 Gr. C carbon steel piping having a 24" ID, 30" OD, and 2.75" wall thickness with a 0.25" thick SA-312 TP304 stainless-steel ID cladding. It is anticipated that the RCS pipe cladding will cover the two piping weld ends.

entries.section_title: Welding of Pump Casing Nozzles to RCS Piping
entries.text: The Supplier shall anticipate that austenitic safe ends (SA-182 Gr. 316L) will be necessary to be welded to both pump casing nozzles. The cladding of the pump casing shall cover the casing nozzle inner side as well as the area where the welding will be performed. In this way, the welding between the safe ends and the pump casing will be standard butt-welding between two austenitic stainless steels.

entries.section_title: Welding of Pump Casing Nozzles to RCS Piping
entries.text: The Supplier may propose alternate weld configurations not using safe ends, such as by butting both butt-welding ends with a nickel-based alloy, or by back gouging. In any case, the final RCP nozzle to RCS piping closure weld design shall strive to avoid dissimilar metal welds having different coefficients of thermal expansion, while ensuring sound weld quality and maximum joint strengths.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: The RCP motors are not required to be operational after a SSE.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: Each SMR-300 RCP pump motor shall be designed in accordance with the parameters contained in Appendix D. Motors shall be suitable for continuous operation at the design external (ambient) conditions inside Containment at 100% reactor power that are listed in Appendix D, specifically including 100% humidity. These are the ambient conditions that are expected at the pump assembly operating locations during the entire plant lifetime.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: RCP motors shall conform to the appropriate provisions of ANSI/NEMA Standard MG 1-2021.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: The motor shall be the squirrel-cage induction type with a drip-proof enclosure.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: The motor shall be suitable for "Unusual Service Conditions" per MG 1-2021 Section 20.28.3, specifically as to exposure to nuclear radiation.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: The motor stator connections shall be the star (wye) type with one end of each of the three windings connected to a common point (neutral), forming a "Y" shape, while the other ends of the windings are connected to the three-phase VAC power supply.

entries.text: The pump casings constitute part of the RCS pressure boundary. They are designated as nuclear safety-related and must be designed and manufactured in accordance with ASME Section III Class 1 and 10CFR50 Appendix B. 10CFR Part 21 for the reporting of defects and noncompliance applies.

The pump casing can be loosely defined as that part of the pump structure which encases the impeller and diffuser and includes the suction and discharge nozzles. The casing serves two main purposes: 1. It is the primary pressure containment; and 2. It gives proper direction to the flow as the fluid passes through the pump.

The suction nozzle directs fluid to the impeller inlet. The impeller discharge is collected, diffused, and directed to the discharge nozzle by the casing. The Holtec SMR-300 RCP casings are to be the diffuser type.

The RCP casings will be butt-welded to 24" ID, 30" OD, 2.75" wall thickness SA-106 Gr. C carbon steel RCS piping having a 0.250" thick SA-312 TP304 stainless-steel ID cladding. Refer to Section 14.2.20 of this Specification for further information on welding the pump casings to the RCS piping.

Pump casing, impeller, and diffuser materials may be castings or forgings and shall utilize the following ASME Section II materials: 1) Casting (stainless-steel): SA-351, Gr. CF8M 2) Casting (carbon steel): SA-216, Gr. WCB 3) Forging (stainless-steel): SA-182, Gr. F316 or F6NM 4) Forging (carbon steel): SA-105, SA-266 Gr. II, or SA-508 Gr. 3 (Class 1) with an internal stainless-steel cladding* *If a stainless-steel clad carbon steel casing is used, the following requirements apply: (a) The cladding shall be performed by weld deposit with austenitic stainless steel (Gr. 316, or 309L/308L). (b) The carbon content, as measured at the surface of the cladding, shall not exceed 0.10%. (c) The final cladding thickness shall be ¼" (0.250") minimum. Forgings are the most preferred option. The Supplier shall justify their selection of castings over forgings and shall receive Buyer Technical Contact approval prior to the

manufacture of any cast steel components. Refer to Section 14.2.12 of this Specification for additional material requirements, including requirements when proposing the substitution of materials other than those specified above.

The pump casing design corrosion allowance shall be 0.032" (minimum) except if ASME Section III requires a higher value otherwise. The pump casings and impellers will process water with the chemistry composition as indicated in Appendix D. It must be assured that the pump can operate or sit stagnant in high boric acid concentrations (up to 2,600 ppm) with no adverse long-term effects, e.g., pitting corrosion or any other loss of pressure boundary material.

To reduce the buildup of corrosion products and improve the future ability to decontaminate the interior of the casings, the casings' interior stainless steel shall be electro-polished and passivated. The intent is to significantly reduce the radiation dose to ALARA levels for personnel during pump and motor maintenance activities.

It is noted that the initial average surface roughness (Ra) of forged or cast stainless steel can vary based on the manufacturing process, machining, and finishing. The electropolishing process typically results in a roughness reduction of up to 50%. For example, assuming an initial Ra of 80 microinches, after electropolishing the improved Ra would be approximately 40 microinches. The requested criterion for the final polishing would be an approximate 50% reduction from the starting average roughness value. The Code required minimum wall thickness for the casings and the specified cladding thickness shall be maintained after electropolishing.

The Buyer requires the pump assembly support design to consist of feet integrally attached to the casing. The support system feet must be sufficient to carry the entire weight of the pump and motor and ultimately must be designed to allow for thermal expansion and to withstand the expected operating and SSE loads. The Supplier shall incorporate adequate additional support points into the pump and motor as needed. These support locations must be identified on the design drawings. Additional information on pump and motor supports is contained in Section 14.2.18 of this Specification.

The pump impeller shall be both statically and dynamically balanced for maximum efficiency and smooth operation without detrimental vibrations over the entire range of anticipated operations, including extended times at low speeds and during speed increases of up to 125% of rated speed.
The rotating element shall be mechanically balanced to preclude vibration.

The pump assembly shall be hydraulically balanced by design and shall include use of flow splitters/straighteners if necessary, also to preclude vibration. 15.0 PUMP ASSEMBLY TESTING
15.1 Pre-Delivery Performance (Factory Acceptance) Testing

Pumps that are considered by the Supplier to be "first-of-a-kind" (FOAK) shall be performance tested to establish that the design meets all functional requirements. This testing shall be performed prior to delivery and is subject to the Buyer's approval. If a Supplier's existing pump design with long-term, successful operating experience in existing LWRs will be provided for the Holtec SMR-300 RCPs, then first-of-a-kind testing may be limited in scope or eliminated. However, a detailed technical justification is expected, i.e., any changes in the provided Holtec SMR-300 pump design from the pre-existing design need to be individually evaluated to assure the operating experience remains applicable.

Each first-of-a-kind pump design or significantly modified pump design shall be performance tested during hot and cold conditions as well as when starting cold and moving up through temperatures and as different speeds, to establish that the design meets all functional requirements. In particular, this testing shall:
Include at least 500 hours of typical in-plant operation (e.g., at actual temperature, pressure, head, flow, and water chemistry).

Include transients and upsets of sufficient number and severity (within the practical limitations of full-scale testing facilities) to provide assurance that the design requirements will be met in actual service.

Include demonstration that the leakage through the seals under loss of all AC power will be limited as specified (this demonstration may be performed using a test fixture rather than a complete pump).
Include complete disassembly and inspection after test.

The specific required tests are divided into three general categories: RCP hydraulic performance, motor performance, and operation transient performance tests, consisting of no less than the following listed tests. Testing is to be conducted at the specified NOP/NOT conditions. These tests, in aggregate, constitute "factory acceptance testing" (FAT).

instruction:
You are requirements management expert. You will be given a document; your goal is to extract text from the document section by section, classify
    whether the text represements a requirement or not, and return a json object with the following schema:
    {
        "title": "...",
        "entries": [
            {
            "doc_title": "...",
            "page_number": ...,
            "section_title": "...",
            "text": "...",
            "is_requirement": "..."
            }
        ],
        "meta": {
            "pages": [..., ...],
        }
    }
    The keys in the output json signify the following:
    - title is the document title, this will be the same as doc_title in the entries list for all entries.
    - entries is a list of sections extracted from the text. Each entry will have:
      > doc_title is the title of the overall document
      > page_number is the page from which the section was extracted (typically displayed at the bottom of pages)
      > section_title is the title of the section extracted. These may or may not be numbered. If they are numbered, numbers should be included
      > text is the full text of the section extracted
      > is_requirement represents your determination as to whether or not the section contains requirement statements
    - meta is an object which contains a list of page numbers. These page numbers should be a set of all page_number values that appear in entries
    
    A requirement typically describes an expected system behavior, capability, constraint, rule, or condition that is intended to guide design, development, or verification.
    Requirement statements often include words such as "shall", "must", "will", or "is required to", but the absence of these keywords does NOT automatically mean the sentence is not a requirement.
    Conversely, sentences that do contain these keywords may not be requirements if they are purely descriptive, explanatory, or context-based.
    In particular, paragraphs that contain the keyword "requirements" may act as introductions to a list of requirements to follow, and should not be marked as requirements themselves.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: PS-8002-0029, Revision 0.0

Cold Performance Characteristics Testing. "Cold coolant" exists with no initial flow when the first RCP is started with the coolant having a specific gravity of approximately 1.0 and a temperature of 100 °F.
Hot Performance Characteristics Testing
Electrical Balance Testing
Heat Insulation Resistance Testing

Service Cycle Testing – to include: start/stop cycles, load variations, operating runs, temperature monitoring, vibration and noise testing, efficiency and performance tests, electrical and mechanical stress testing, leakage and seal integrity, shutdowns and stops.
Pressure Pulsation Measurement Testing
Reduced Voltage Hang Up Testing
Loss of Power Testing
Loss of External Cooling Water Testing
Operational / Endurance Testing
Reverse Rotation Operability Testing
Forward Restart of Reverse Rotating Testing
Net Positive Suction Head Testing
Coast Down Testing to Complete Stop – time required between natural frequency and operating speed.
Overspeed and Critical Speed Testing – Verification of ± 25% separation margin between natural frequency and operating speed.
Flow Induced Vibration Testing. Confirm that the assembly can operate within vibration limits set by industry standards (ISO 10816 and/or API-610).

If the Supplier is unable to test at NOP/NOT conditions, then the Supplier is to explain in detail the analytical methods for the reliable and accurate extrapolation of cold or low-speed test data to hot or high-speed conditions. The Supplier shall consider the use of the following analytical methods:

Modal Analysis Identifies the natural frequencies, mode shapes, and damping ratios of the pump and its components. This analysis helps in understanding how the pump structure vibrates at different frequencies and is crucial for avoiding resonance conditions.

Harmonic Analysis Assesses the pump’s response to sinusoidal loads at various frequencies. This is important for understanding how operational forces (such as those from rotating imbalances or fluid flow pulsations) might induce vibrations.

Transient Dynamic Analysis Evaluates the pump’s response to time-varying loads during start-up, shutdown, and coastdown. This analysis can predict how the pump will behave under sudden changes in conditions, which are critical for safety assessments.

Assesses the mechanical integrity of the pump under static and dynamic loads, considering the effects of vibration-induced stresses. This analysis helps in ensuring that the pump structure can withstand the operational loads without failure.

Evaluates the interaction between the fluid flow within the pump and the pump structure itself. This complex analysis is vital for understanding the impact of fluid dynamics on vibration behavior and vice versa
Motors shall be tested per IEEE 112-2017. Testing shall also meet the applicable provisions of Part 20 of ANSI/NEMA Standard MG 1-2021.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The type of RCPs to be procured is a vertical motor-driven single stage centrifugal shaft-sealed pump assembly with bottom suction and radial discharge having a controlled or limited leakage pump shaft sealing system, as further described below.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The main components of shaft-sealed pumps are the pump case assembly, the pump cover and heat exchanger assembly, the driver mount, the rotating element assembly (shaft, impeller, and couplings) and the shaft seal assembly. The pump driver consists of a squirrel-cage AC induction type motor. The shaft seal assembly is to include a small coil-type heat exchanger, a shaft mounted auxiliary impeller, multiple mechanical seals, and seal pressure breakdown devices. The seal assembly functions to minimize the leakage of reactor coolant past the shaft and into the containment structure (CS). A flywheel is to be installed on the motor rotor to increase pump coast down time after a loss of electrical power with the plant at full power. The shaft-sealed RCPs are to be mounted vertically with the motor on top of the pump assembly with the casing on the bottom welded to the RCS cold leg piping.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump assemblies to be provided under this project shall comply with all the detailed requirements of this Specification. The selected Supplier will be responsible for meeting the requirements of the regulatory agencies specified herein, including the obtaining of certifications and stampings which indicate such compliance, as well as any ancillary agencies. The selected Supplier will ultimately be responsible for the overall design, procurement of materials, fabrication, testing, cleaning, packaging, and shipping of the complete pump assemblies, including any specialized tooling and necessary spare parts.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: It should be noted that since the Holtec SMR-300 is a new plant design, US NRC interactions may be required depending on the Supplier's design, analytical methods, and test methods or results. The Supplier may be required to provide licensing support to address US NRC Requests for Information (RFIs) or topical report generation.
The current project working schedule requires delivery of the pump assemblies to the SMR-300 plant location in Covert, Michigan as follows:
Table 10-1: Required Delivery Dates for the Pump Assemblies
Pumps 1 and 2 for Unit 1
Spare Rotating Element Assembly
1 Refer to Appendix D for Equipment Identification (Tag) Numbers. The spare rotating element assembly does not have a specific plant ID number.

The Supplier providing these items must be on Holtec's Approved Vendor List (AVL) prior to beginning work. The Supplier's Quality Assurance program and manufacturing facilities must be audited successfully by the Buyer to be placed on the AVL. This audit will include on-site review of the Supplier's facilities by an Audit Team. Placement of the Supplier on the Holtec AVL is at the sole discretion of the Holtec Corporate QA Manager.

The RCPs under this Purchase Specification are subject to 10CFR50 Appendix B and shall be designed, manufactured, and tested under a Nuclear Quality Assurance Program in compliance with the Supplier's Buyer-approved ASME NQA-1 Program.

The Supplier shall state their corporate Quality Assurance Program applicable to performance of the scope of work. The Supplier shall submit their Quality Assurance Program Manual, quality inspection plans, quality inspection procedures, field test and inspection plans, and field test and inspection procedures for the Buyer's review and acceptance prior to proceeding with the relevant activities.

All work shall be compliant to 10CFR50 Appendix B and ASME NQA-1 requirements under the Supplier's Buyer-approved NQA-1 program. Exceptions may be considered on a case-by-case basis, with Supplier requests submitted formally as a Change Order or Revision Request. If the Supplier is unable to perform the specified work under its Buyer-approved Quality Assurance Program, the Buyer may alternatively extend its own nuclear Quality Assurance Program as necessary, or alternatively, decline the Supplier's request.
All work shall be performed under KSB's ASME certificates N-2795 and/or N-2796. These ASME certificates shall remain valid during all phases of this project.

The Supplier shall possess valid ASME Certificate of Authorizations to apply U-Stamps (Pressure Vessels) and N-Stamps (Nuclear Components). Engineering scope under the jurisdiction of ASME Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code shall be stamped as per the requirements of ASME Section III Subsection NCA once the work is finally approved. entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The upper horizontal support element (collar) for each RCP's lateral supports (snubbers) shall be located on the pumps such that the snubbers can be connected from the collar to the adjacent concrete slab at plant elevation (El.) -22'-0" (refer to Appendix B).

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: To ensure structural integrity and stability, the composite pump assembly support structure must be robust enough to bear the weight of the pump, motor, and any associated components, as well as dynamic forces during operation. Specific load combinations that need to be considered include dead loads, live loads, thermal loads, seismic loads, and dynamic loads due to pump operation.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The design of pump supports must ensure structural integrity under normal, upset, emergency, and faulted conditions.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump supporting structure shall permit the entire pump assembly to endure the SSE loads specified in Section 14.8 of this Specification.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Proper alignment between the pump and motor is crucial to prevent excessive wear and tear on the bearings and other components. Pump supports shall allow for the needed adjustments by the Buyer to maintain precise alignment and leveling. The support attachment points must ultimately allow for free (equal) thermal movements between the RPV nozzles and the RCP nozzles.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Materials used for the support structure shall be resistant to corrosion or otherwise be coated per Section 14.10 of this Specification, due to the harsh environmental conditions and corrosiveness of the pumped fluid. Consideration shall be given to the thermal expansion and contraction of materials used in the pump and support structure, and any of their coatings, due to the range of ambient and fluid temperatures.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The supporting structure shall prevent excessive vibrations, which can lead to mechanical failures, noise, and reduced pump life. The support structure shall be designed to absorb or isolate vibrations generated during pump operation. To minimize vibration transmission to the foundation and/or surrounding structures, vibration isolators or dampeners shall be included in the supporting design as needed.

Pump nozzle loads must be evaluated under various load combinations as specified in ASME Section III, NB-3200 (Design by Analysis) and NB-3600 (Piping Design). These combinations include dead loads, pressure loads, thermal loads, seismic loads, and other dynamic effects.

The Supplier shall provide the pump nozzle loads and load combinations to the Buyer to allow the Buyer to analyze and properly design the connected RCS piping and piping supports. The Buyer will notify the Supplier if the final piping design results in increased loads on the pump nozzles.

Proper alignment between the pump and motor is crucial to prevent excessive wear and tear on the bearings and other components. Pump supports shall allow for the needed adjustments by the Buyer to maintain precise alignment and leveling. The support attachment points must ultimately allow for free (equal) thermal movements between the RPV nozzles and the RCP nozzles. Materials used for the support structure shall be resistant to corrosion or otherwise be coated per Section 14.10 of this Specification, due to the harsh environmental conditions and corrosiveness of the pumped fluid. Consideration shall be given to the thermal expansion and contraction of materials used in the pump and support structure, and any of their coatings, due to the range of ambient and fluid temperatures. The support structure shall be designed to absorb or isolate vibrations generated during pump operation. To minimize vibration transmission to the foundation and/or surrounding structures, vibration isolators or dampeners shall be included in the supporting design as needed.

Pump nozzle loads must be evaluated under various load combinations as specified in ASME Section III, NB-3200 (Design by Analysis) and NB-3600 (Piping Design). These combinations include dead loads, pressure loads, thermal loads, seismic loads, and other dynamic effects. The Supplier shall provide the pump nozzle loads and load combinations to the Buyer to allow the Buyer to analyze and properly design the connected RCS piping and piping supports. The Buyer will notify the Supplier if the final piping design results in increased loads on the pump nozzles.

entries.text: The pump shaft and drive shaft are to be connected by a metallic splined face, rigid flange coupling to ensure positive reproducibility of shaft alignment. The motor drive shaft is to be coupled to the pump drive shaft by a metallic curved tooth coupling.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump shaft assembly couplings are to be designed to compensate for angular and/or radial misalignments to minimize the thrust transmitted to the motor, and to facilitate pump shaft assembly in the field and pump motor changeouts.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The critical speed is the speed at which the shaft assembly's natural frequency matches the rotational speed, causing resonance. The damped natural frequency of the RCP rotating assembly shall be at least 25% above or 25% below the operating speed to avoid resonance (i.e., a ± 25% separation margin). Modal damping shall be evaluated in accordance with API 610 (12th Edition) to prevent adverse effects.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump shaft and drive shaft materials shall be ASME SA-182 F6NM forgings, or ASME SA-743 CA6NM or ASME SA-487 CA6NM castings, or other Buyer approved materials with equivalent chemical composition, mechanical properties, and corrosion resistance. Pump shafts shall be solid material not hollow.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The Supplier shall perform finite element analyses (FEA) to ensure that the probability of a complete pump shaft shear during all phases of pump operations is less than 10-6 events per reactor year.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Reactor coolant pumps are to utilize shaft seals which are designed to limit the leakage to containment of reactor coolant along the pump shaft. This is to be achieved by using a series of primary and secondary seals. These seals essentially become part of the safety-related reactor coolant system pressure boundary and shall be designed and manufactured in accordance with a 10CFR50 Appendix B QA Program. The primary seals (e.g., metallic oxides, carbides, and graphite, etc.) will limit the leakage of reactor coolant across the interface between rotating and stationary RCS elements. The secondary seals (e.g., elastomer O-rings, U-cups, and channel seals, etc.) will prevent leakage between stationary mechanical elements of the RCS seal or those elements that have only a slight relative motion. The Supplier shall delineate the specific safety-classification of each of the seal components that is required to maintain the RCS pressure boundary safety function.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Pump design shall incorporate hydrodynamic cartridge seal packages. A unit seal cartridge which can be brought into the containment as a complete unit is required to reduce the impact on seal replacement time and plant availability by eliminating the handling the seals within containment in more than one piece.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The minimum design life objective for controlled leakage seals is 50,000 hours of operation at NOP/NOT. Shaft seal life shall be demonstrated either by prior PWR plant experience or by realistic long-term tests of the seals (minimum of 6,000 hours).

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The shaft system shall be designed to allow continued operation of the pump for a period of at least one week, but preferably longer, after failure of one of the several stages in order to permit an orderly plant shutdown, without excessive loss of reactor coolant, in the event of the degradation of a second seal stage. In addition, a backup stage capable of holding against full pressure with the pump idle shall be provided. The required holding time and allowable leakage rate for the backup seal is 168 hours at a maximum leak rate of 1.0 gpm. Seals shall comply with U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) Order EA-12-049 endorsed in JLD-ISG-2012-01 (Feb. 2017).

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Normal operation of the seal package, including anticipated fluctuations in seal boundary conditions such as fluid temperature or pressure, shall not result in inter-seal cavity pressure oscillations in multi-stage seals.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The seal package shall withstand the extended low-pressure operation expected to occur in actual service without damage (e.g., during startup) which would otherwise prevent the seal package from attaining its design life.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Stress and deflection analyses of all seal parts shall be performed to show that no undesired interferences or excessive O-ring extrusion gaps occur as a result of deflections due to mechanical and pressure loadings and temperature changes and that the stresses in the parts are within allowable values. These analyses shall account for worst-case fabrication tolerances and for anticipated operating conditions, including off-normal events and the resultant transient conditions in the seal.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Seals are to be qualified to prevent significant shaft leakage at NOP/NOT during Station Blackout (SBO) conditions, i.e., loss of all electrical power and cooling water (seal injection and CCW) for a period of 72 hours minimum to assure safe plant shutdown. This plant injection design condition is termed "extended loss of AC power" (ELAP).

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: RCPs are to be designed with a backseat provision when the pump is uncoupled from the motor. The backseat design provides a RCS pressure boundary to permit replacement of the seal package and/or motor during plant outages when the refueling cavity is fully filled with water. The weight of the impeller/shaft assembly shall be sufficient to provide pressure boundary control for this maintenance activity. The required static head is estimated to be at least 35 feet of water (approximately 15 psi). It is expected, barring wear, erosion, or imperfect sealing of the backseat seals, that there would be no more than 0-1 gpm continuous leakage in the backseated position. Minimization of backseat leakage is important to prevent both inadvertent draindown of the RCS and to reduce radiation doses to maintenance workers replacing pump seals. The Supplier is to provide the static head value that could lift the assembly off its backseat causing cavity leakage into the maintenance area.

entries.section_title: 15.3 ASME B&PV Code In-Service Inspection (ISI) and In-Service Testing (IST)
entries.text: The RCP assemblies in this Specification are classified as ASME B&PV Section III Code Class 1 and thus must be designed and provided with adequate physical access to enable the performance of the required Inservice Inspection (ISI) activities that are specified in Subsection IWB of the 2017 Edition of Section XI, as well as to permit Inservice Testing of the pumps for assessing operational readiness, as set forth in the ASME OM Code Division 1 Section IST (2009 Edition).

entries.section_title: 15.3 ASME B&PV Code In-Service Inspection (ISI) and In-Service Testing (IST)
entries.text: Design provisions shall be provided to permit the disassembly of the pump internals and motor, for inspection of the pump casing, pressure boundary welds, as well as bearings, flywheel assembly, and other internal components to facilitate the required Section XI and OM Code inspections.

Site Acceptance Testing is required to ensure each pump is installed, integrated, and performs as intended under actual site conditions. SAT verifies compliance with nuclear industry standards, technical specifications, plant safety requirements, and operational criteria before commissioning.

Site acceptance testing will be performed by Holtec at the Palisades plant location after final installation of the pumps in the Reactor Coolant System at each unit. Holtec has the primary responsibility for the overseeing and conducting of all site acceptance testing.
It is expected that SAT at the Palisades site will include the following activities:
The Supplier shall support the Palisades site acceptance testing by:

The spare parts list shall include notation of the Quality classification of each part, i.e., nuclear safety-related or commercial grade.
2. The spare parts list shall be itemized into the following categories:
a. Pump (hydraulic) section
b. Mechanical seal system
f. Oil lubrication system
g. Spare parts for special tools

3. When authorized by a formal Purchase Order from the Buyer, the Supplier shall provide the recommended spare parts in the quantities listed on the Purchase Order and deliver all items per the purchase order’s schedule requirements.
4. All ordered parts shall be robustly packaged to prevent damage during transit. Parts packages shall include the following information, at a minimum:
a. Buyer’s Purchase Order Number
d. Quantity and unit of measure
e. Applicable pump or motor model number
f. Supplier’s drawing number and BOM item number
g. Applicable documentation, such as: certified material test reports (CMTRs) and Certificates of Conformance, etc.
h. Special storage information (as applicable) such as: shelf-life limitations, required storage environmental conditions, and in-storage maintenance requirements

entries.text: The range limits for RCP component cooling water and seal injection water temperatures, rates of change of temperature, and the limits for the maximum allowable filtered particle size of the supplied water shall be as listed in Appendix D of this Specification.

[1] The materials of all pump hydraulic pressure-retaining parts in direct contact with the reactor coolant must conform with the requirements set forth in Section III of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, 2021 Edition. ASME Section III requires the use of the materials listed in ASME Section II. Other materials of the pump must conform to the requirements of the specifications for materials listed in this Code. The requirements of USNRC Regulatory Guide (RG) 1.84, "Design, Fabrication, and Materials Code Case Acceptability; ASME Section III" shall also apply.

[2] If other than ASME Section III/II listed materials are to be used for primary pressure-retaining parts (e.g., ISO, EN, RCC-M, etc.), a formal ASME code reconciliation as described in Subsection NCA is required to demonstrate equivalency for each substitution. All such analyses shall be included in the pump assembly's documentation package.

[3] The ASME Section III/II material requirements and code reconciliation requirements in [2] above do not apply to items that are not associated with the pressure-retaining function of the pump, such as shafts, trim, bearings, bushings, wear plates, seals, packing, and gaskets.
[4] Piping materials for the CVC, CCW and motor lube oil cooling piping shall comply with ASME B31.1-2022 requirements.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: PS-8002-0029, Revision 0.0

Generally, the RCP assemblies shall be constructed with only materials which have been proven by experience to be suitable for light water reactor (LWR) service. Materials which have seen little or no LWR service are not entirely prohibited, but proven materials are preferred. A written justification for the use of unproven materials, or for the use of materials not contained in ASME Section II, shall be provided. The justification shall discuss why the listed or unproven material is being selected and the basis on which the Supplier considers it to be acceptable. This justification should address peak stresses and strains, local water chemistry, expected radiation environment, and temperature at the point of specific application.

In general, all pump parts except the bearings and seal faces that are in contact with the reactor coolant and injection water should be of austenitic or other stainless steel, Inconel, or an equivalent corrosion resistant material. Carbon and alloy steels with weld-deposited austenitic stainless steel or non-air-hardening Inconel cladding are acceptable for pressure boundary parts. The carbon content measured at the surface of the cladding must not exceed 0.10%.

Pump parts not in contact with the reactor coolant must be of a corrosion-resistant material or otherwise coated per Section 14.10 of this Specification. All materials in contact with RCS, CVC, and CCW fluids must be compatible with all other supplied materials to not cause cathodic corrosion concerns.

RCS piping chemical decontamination will be required periodically over the plant life to minimize personnel radiation exposures. All reactor coolant pump parts wetted by primary coolant shall be compatible with standard PWR chemical decontamination solutions.

It is anticipated that standard PWR chemical decontamination solutions will be periodically utilized over the plant's life. Decontamination processes that may be used include but are not limited to: CANDEREM (citric acid and EDTA), CITROX (citric acid and oxalic acid), NITROX / NITROX-E (nitric acid, oxalic acid and potassium permanganate). Frequency of decontamination will depend on plant needs to keep the primary piping and RCP casing dose rates as low as reasonably achievable (ALARA). Decontamination will be performed when needed during plant outages to the specific process and quantities of the chemicals used will depend on the isotopes to be removed and the radiation dose reduction required.

In the event compatibility with the anticipated chemical decontamination solutions cannot be achieved, incompatible parts shall be designed to either be removed from the pump or otherwise have provisions allowing isolation from the decontamination solution. Such parts shall be clearly delineated on the Supplier's design drawings.
The allowable heating and cooling rate of parts exposed to the high temperature reactor coolant shall be at least 100 °F/hr.

entries.text: 1. Design, procurement, and manufacturing records for nuclear safety-related components must be retained by the Supplier for the entire operational lifetime of the nuclear plant and of each component.
2. Non-safety-related documentation shall be maintained by the Supplier for a minimum of 10 years.

The Holtec SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps (RCPs) are major components of the plant's Reactor Coolant System (RCS). The RCS consists of the Reactor Pressure Vessel (RPV), a single once-through Steam Generator (SG) with an integrally connected Pressurizer, and two RCPs. Each pump is located in an individual cold leg between the SG and RPV. There will be two separate hot legs between the RPV and SG. Refer to Figure 12-1 below for a simplified flow diagram (the hot legs are shown in red, and the cold legs are shown in blue). Refer to Appendix A for a conceptual RCS equipment layout drawing. Refer to Appendix B for draft equipment layout within the SMR-300 containment.
Figure 12-1 Simplified Holtec SMR-300 RCS

The cold legs will be constructed from SA-106 Gr. C carbon steel piping having a 24" inside diameter, 30" outside diameter, 2.75" wall thickness, and a 0.250" thick SA-312 TP304 stainless-steel interior cladding. Cold leg design pressure and temperature are 2,485 psig and 650 °F, respectively. At 100% reactor power, normal operating pressure (NOP) and normal operating temperature (NOT) in the RCS cold legs are 2,250 psia and approximately 546 °F, respectively.

The reactor coolant consists of demineralized water containing a maximum of 2,500 ppm to 2,600 ppm of boric acid at beginning of core life (BOL). During cold conditions at this concentration, the added boric acid does not appreciably affect the specific gravity (SG) of the demineralized water, i.e., the specific gravity remains at approximately 1.0. For the specified

The Holtec SMR-300 RCPs are necessary to provide sufficient flow during normal power operations to ensure adequate heat is transferred from the reactor core within the RPV to the Steam Generator via the reactor coolant water. The specific purposes of the RCPs are:
To provide the forced circulation of reactor coolant for the removal of core heat;
Maintain the departure from nucleate boiling ratio (DNBR) within the acceptable range during pump coast down after loss of all supplied reactor coolant pump motor electrical power; and
To provide energy to heat up the RCS from ambient temperature to greater than the minimum temperature required for criticality prior to reactor startup.
The Holtec SMR-300 RCPs have two safety-related functions:
The RCPs serve as part of the RCS pressure boundary for containing the reactor coolant; and
The RCPs maintain the minimum necessary reactor flow for a defined time while coasting down after a loss of off-site power (LOOP) event with reactor trip.

The two RCPs are an integral part of the reactor coolant pressure boundary. The pumps are required to be designed, fabricated, and tested to quality standards consistent with the requirements set forth in the ASME B&PV Code Section III Division 1 for Class 1 components (Subsection NB) 2021 Edition, 10CFR50 Appendix B, ASME NQA-1, 10CFR50.55a, and 10CFR50 Appendix A General Design Criteria (GDC).

It should be noted that 10CFR50 Appendix A provides design criteria for the RCP design organization (Holtec International). These requirements are extended to the RCP design organization (Supplier) by means of this Specification, although the Buyer retains ultimate design responsibility. The 10CFR50 Appendix A design criteria specifically applicable to the Reactor Coolant Pumps include: 1, 2, 3, 4, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 30, 31, and 32.

entries.section_title: 14.2 Design Requirements for Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The Holtec SMR-300 RCPs shall meet all the following general and specific design requirements. These requirements are all listed in order of importance.

Pumps are expected to normally only pump single phase flow (i.e., compressed water) at NOP/NOT. However, during accident conditions (e.g., a sudden RCS system pressure decrease), and possibly during normal start-up and shut-down, two-phase flow conditions may occur. These two-phase flow conditions may result in flashing and vapor (steam) formation in the pump casings. Pump design shall be robust in order to prevent pump damage from the potential vibration and shock of hydraulic surges that may occur during temporary two-phase flow conditions. Pump design robustness in the case of two-phase flows should specifically address areas such as:

Two-phase flow conditions are only expected to occur during Design Basis Accident (DBA) conditions such as medium to large LOCA or a Main Steam Line Break (MSLB). These events are not expected to occur during the life of the plant. The RCP will not be operated during or following DBAs and is therefore not required to be designed by the Supplier to operate during these periods.

During RCP start-up, localized two-phase flow can occur around the pump vanes due to cavitation if the pump operates close to the vapor pressure of the coolant. The RCP is most susceptible to cavitation at startup due to low RCS system pressures while performing heat-up operations, potentially resulting in inadequate net positive suction head (NPSH). The Supplier shall ensure adequate NPSH requirements to prevent pump internals damage.

It is important for reactor protection purposes that the reactor coolant continues to flow for a short and well-defined time after a loss of pump motor electrical power with subsequent reactor trip. To provide for this flow, each reactor coolant pump, regardless of design variation, shall contain a high-density flywheel and high-inertia motor. The rotating inertia of the pump, motor, and flywheel will be used during the coast down period to continue the reactor coolant flow. The

gradual decrease in flow (coast down) improves the Departure from Nucleate Boiling Ratio (DNBR) after a complete loss of pumping power event. Since the flywheel is involved in reactor protection analysis, it is nuclear safety-related and is subject to periodic regulatory required integrity inspections, and thus must be designed to easily permit such inspections. 10CFR Part 21 for the reporting of defects and non-compliance applies to the flywheel.

Each reactor coolant pump shall have the coast down characteristics specified in Appendix D which assure adequate RCS flow during pump coast down after interruption of power to the pump motor. This ensures thermal margins in the core following pump trip.

Adequate rotational inertia shall be provided by the pump-motor assembly itself, preferably without special internal configurations which add inertia. Permanently connected rotating machinery shall not be used to effectively increase the inertia and decrease the rate of coast down. That is, the use of either external flywheels or electrically connected rotating machinery is prohibited, since extra rotating equipment and electrical connections will add complexity to the plant and will add to the in-service inspection and maintenance burdens.

The determination of required rotational inertia shall account for operation of the pumps with dips in grid frequency. Pumps shall be designed to continue operation under off normal frequency conditions. It is possible for the voltage at the terminals of the pumps to vary from 100% to 85% of rated. For the Palisades SMR-300 site, the design shall be for a frequency range of 57.6 Hz to 61.2 Hz @ 85% rated voltage. On a loss of all VAC power, Appendix D identifies a coastdown requirement of 30% flow @ 30 seconds. Pump motors should be capable of indefinite operation at 85% voltage and @ 57.6 Hz.
Compliance with the following requirements shall apply to the pump assembly flywheel(s):
2. 10CFR50 Appendix A General Design Criteria 1 and 4
3. NRC Regulatory Guide 1.14 Rev. 1
4. NRC Standard Review Plan (NUREG-0800 Rev. 3) Section 5.4.1.1

Pump assembly design shall be such where the flywheel is enclosed wholly within the pump motors. The use of flywheels external to the pump or motor assemblies or located within the pump casing themselves (internal) is prohibited.
Mechanical stresses on the entire pump assembly during pump start-ups shall be considered in the determination of the final flywheel size, material, mass, and moments of inertia.

The Supplier shall analyze and document that in the event of a flywheel failure, the surrounding motor housing components are adequate to prevent missiles from jeopardizing the structural integrity of the reactor coolant system and other plant structures, systems and components. The analysis shall provide certification that the RCP flywheel and motor housing were analyzed to demonstrate that a fractured flywheel cannot potentially impair the operation of nearby safety-related systems or components.

entries.text: This Purchase Specification provides the technical, documentation, and quality assurance requirements for the design, manufacture, testing, and shipment of complete Reactor Coolant Pump (RCP) assemblies for Holtec’s SMR-300 advanced nuclear power electrical generation station. "Pump assemblies" in this document refers to the entire manufactured component, i.e., the hydraulic pump section joined with the motor section.

SMR, LLC, based in Camden, NJ, is a wholly owned subsidiary of Holtec International and is the owner and designer of the two-unit SMR-300 plant site planned to be constructed at the existing Palisades nuclear plant site in Covert, Michigan where the RCP assemblies are to be installed.

This document supplements the formal Purchase Order (PO) between the selected Supplier (KSB) and Holtec International ("Buyer") and has been prepared in accordance with Holtec procedure HSP-100402, "Purchase Specifications", Revision 4.

The Supplier shall furnish Reactor Coolant pumps and motors, spare parts and tooling in the quantities and per the schedule delineated in the Purchase Order, in accordance with all agreed upon Terms and Conditions attached to the Purchase Order. The pump assemblies shall be complete with all associated supporting systems and instrumentation defined herein.

The Supplier shall be responsible for design, engineering, manufacturing, including supply, and assembly of equipment, the supply of drawings and data, all sub-Supplier coordination, inspection, testing, cleaning, packaging, and shipping of each pump assembly and all items included in the scope of this equipment specification. The Supplier shall deliver all equipment to the Buyer in accordance with the agreed upon delivery schedule.

The Holtec SMR-300 is a small modular reactor (SMR) nuclear electrical generating station with an output of approximately 300 MW electrical (MWe) per unit. It is an advanced pressurized water reactor (PWR) plant based on existing light water reactor (LWR) technologies consisting of two reactor coolant loops with a common steam generator. Each reactor coolant loop will contain one RCP. The SMR-300 station for which the RCPs are to be provided will consist of two units which will be constructed and located in Covert, Michigan at the same site as the existing Palisades Nuclear Plant. The station will be licensed under current US NRC regulations codified principally in Title 10 CFR Part 50.

The output of each of the two reactor cores is approximately 1,050 MW thermal (MWt). The units are designed for a nominal 18-month refueling cycle with flexibility for longer or shorter cycles depending upon the operating utility’s requirements. The overall plant design life is 80 years.

The following codes, standards, and regulations apply to the extent as indicated in this Purchase Specification. Except where explicitly specified otherwise in this Specification or, in cases of discrepancies, as otherwise specified in Holtec Report No. HI-2240448, the latest edition at the time of contract issuance shall apply. Non-cited references are included for information purposes only.

entries.section_title: Welding of Pump Casing Nozzles to RCS Piping
entries.text: For non-Code welding, all weld procedures and welders shall be qualified in accordance with ASME Section IX (2021).

entries.section_title: Welding of Pump Casing Nozzles to RCS Piping
entries.text: The two pump casing nozzles will be butt-welded to the RCS piping by the Buyer during plant construction. Current SMR-300 plant RCS design provides for the cold legs to be constructed from SA-106 Gr. C carbon steel piping having a 24" ID, 30" OD, and 2.75" wall thickness with a 0.25" thick SA-312 TP304 stainless-steel ID cladding. It is anticipated that the RCS pipe cladding will cover the two piping weld ends.

entries.section_title: Welding of Pump Casing Nozzles to RCS Piping
entries.text: The Supplier shall anticipate that austenitic safe ends (SA-182 Gr. 316L) will be necessary to be welded to both pump casing nozzles. The cladding of the pump casing shall cover the casing nozzle inner side as well as the area where the welding will be performed. In this way, the welding between the safe ends and the pump casing will be standard butt-welding between two austenitic stainless steels.

entries.section_title: Welding of Pump Casing Nozzles to RCS Piping
entries.text: The Supplier may propose alternate weld configurations not using safe ends, such as by butting both butt-welding ends with a nickel-based alloy, or by back gouging. In any case, the final RCP nozzle to RCS piping closure weld design shall strive to avoid dissimilar metal welds having different coefficients of thermal expansion, while ensuring sound weld quality and maximum joint strengths.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: The RCP motors are not required to be operational after a SSE.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: Each SMR-300 RCP pump motor shall be designed in accordance with the parameters contained in Appendix D. Motors shall be suitable for continuous operation at the design external (ambient) conditions inside Containment at 100% reactor power that are listed in Appendix D, specifically including 100% humidity. These are the ambient conditions that are expected at the pump assembly operating locations during the entire plant lifetime.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: RCP motors shall conform to the appropriate provisions of ANSI/NEMA Standard MG 1-2021.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: The motor shall be the squirrel-cage induction type with a drip-proof enclosure.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: The motor shall be suitable for "Unusual Service Conditions" per MG 1-2021 Section 20.28.3, specifically as to exposure to nuclear radiation.

entries.section_title: General Design Requirements for RCP Motors
entries.text: The motor stator connections shall be the star (wye) type with one end of each of the three windings connected to a common point (neutral), forming a "Y" shape, while the other ends of the windings are connected to the three-phase VAC power supply.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: PS-8002-0029, Revision 0.0

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump motor is not classified as Class 1E. Environmental and seismic qualification of the motor per the requirements of 10CFR50.49, NRC Regulatory Guide 1.89, and IEEE Standards 323 and 344 are not required.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Motor rating shall be 4160V, 3-phase, 60 cycles per second (Hz) with a Service Factor (SF) of 1.15 (continuous). It is expected that the motor will be normally operated at the nameplate horsepower. It is desired that the motor be capable, when necessary, of an output of 1.15 times the rated horsepower during plant power operations (hot conditions) with the motor provided with nameplate voltage and frequency. The service factor shall not be credited during motor starting and shall only be used to account for occasional overloads under normal running conditions.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: With only 85%-rated voltage available, the pump motor shall be capable of starting the pump in reactor coolant having a 1.0 specific gravity (SG), i.e., cold conditions. It is assumed the pump curve will be developed by the Supplier using a SG of 1.0. Thus, when ensuring satisfactory performance when the motor has only a 85% of rated voltage available, pump performance should be evaluated for pumping fluid with a SG of 1.0.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The motor shall be suitable for "across-the-line" starting with sustained full line voltage.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: It is desired that the pump assemblies be operated at synchronous speeds, i.e., the motor's rotor will spin at the same speed as the stator's rotating magnetic field. The optimum number of motor poles is 6 and the nominal operating motor speed is to be 1,200 rpm to ensure the best overall performance. The selected normal operating speed shall provide for a long motor life with minimal motor maintenance. The pump, motor, and flywheel design maximum speed shall be 125% of the selected normal operating speed. The entire pump assembly shall be capable of operation without mechanical damage at speeds up to, and including, 125% of normal speed.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The temperature rise of the motor when operating with a reactor coolant temperature of 500°F or above shall be in accordance with ANSI/NEMA MG 1-2021. The maximum normal ambient temperature is specified in Appendix D.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The average and hot spot temperatures, considering the effects of extremes of ambient temperatures, cooling water flow and temperature, and power consumption, shall not exceed the temperatures for which the motor insulation has been proven stable in service.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The three (3) stator winding leads shall be brought out into a conduit box mounted on the side of the motor.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Positive means of preventing RCP motor oil leakage from posing a fire hazard within containment as well as from entering the RCP shaft seals shall be provided. Design provisions shall be in accordance with USNRC Regulatory Guide 1.189 Revision 5. The oil collection system should not require removal when removing or installing an RCP shaft seal.

entries.section_title: Means of accurately achieving and verifying motor shaft to pump shaft alignment shall be provided.
entries.text: The required alignment procedure shall not require loosening of the pump closure studs.

entries.section_title: Design provisions to allow "barring over" the pump and motor are desired.
entries.text: This refers to provisions to permit hand turning of the rotor assembly using simple tools, such as a bar, to ensure the rotor is unbound and moves freely prior to starting.

The pump, pump motor, pump shaft, and pump shaft seal shall be capable of being restarted after an indefinite period of time during which the pump has been idle with the reactor coolant system at normal operating pressure and temperature (NOP/NOT). Injection water and cooling water would be supplied to the pump during this period. Acceptable temperatures and temperature distributions shall

The above requirement deals with the loss and restoration of component cooling during Mode 3 "Hot Standby" (i.e., NOP and NOT). The pumps need the ability to be restarted in Mode 3 at NOP/NOT (2250 psia and 557 °F in the RCS be maintained even though the pump is not rotating. The pump design shall permit the loss and restoration of component cooling water while the pump is idle (cold legs) with all auxiliary systems in service (i.e., seal injection, component cooling water, etc.). A pump sitting idle at NOP/NOT shall not result in temperature gradients of pump components that would adversely impact pump starting and hydraulic performance.

Each pump assembly must be capable of standing idle in a partially filled system without requiring any special hydraulic procedures to prevent any adverse conditions that could cause malfunction. Free oxygen and moisture may be in contact with all pump surfaces normally exposed to reactor coolant or component cooling water.
As applicable to the motor type, motors shall be equipped with strip heaters per Section 14.3 of this Specification to prevent condensation during extended lay-up periods.

The reactor coolant pumps will be started and stopped during routine operations such as plant heat-up and cooldown, and in connection with recovery from certain transients such as loss of electrical power. The approximate RCS pressure and temperature conditions under which these operations may occur are as follows:
Cold conditions: 70°F and 100 psig
Pump restart conditions after commencement of heat-up: 100°F and 400 psig
Hot conditions: 557°F and 2,235 psig

The reactor coolant pumps, including the motors, shall be suitable to withstand the normal thermal transients in [1] above experienced by the reactor coolant system as a whole, as well as withstanding the thermal transients associated with:
Starting or stopping the pump without modulation of the flow rate or temperature of seal injection and/or cooling water.

entries.section_title: Finite Element Modeling of Complete Pump Assemblies
entries.text: The Supplier is required to model the complete pump assembly as a "super element" using ANSYS software. The model must accurately represent the pump's physical, mechanical, and dynamic characteristics for use in finite element analysis (FEA) of the overall system in which the pump will be integrated.

entries.section_title: Finite Element Modeling of Complete Pump Assemblies
entries.text: The Supplier shall contact the Buyer's Technical Contact to request any information necessary to complete an accurate model.
Software: ANSYS (latest version compatible with ANSYS Workbench and Mechanical APDL).
Element Type: Super element (substructure) representation.
Degrees of Freedom: Include all relevant degrees of freedom to capture the pump assembly's dynamic behavior.
Material Properties: Accurate material properties, including density, Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, and damping coefficients.
Boundary Conditions: Appropriate boundary conditions reflecting the operational environment.

    Requirement statements often include words such as "shall", "must", "will", or "is required to", but the absence of these keywords does NOT automatically mean the sentence is not a requirement.
    Conversely, sentences that do contain these keywords may not be requirements if they are purely descriptive, explanatory, or context-based.

entries.text: The Supplier shall ensure the pump’s required net positive suction head (NPSHr) is such that the Buyer can assure the design of the RCS tumble margin above the system’s available net positive suction head (NPSHa). This will provide operational integrity and minimize the potential for cavitation.

It should be noted that the Holtec SMR-300 does not require reactor coolant pump operation to achieve safe shut down, and minimum net positive suction head requirements are not required to provide safe operation of the Holtec SMR-300. However, the margin between the required net positive suction head (NPSHr) and available net positive suction head (NPSHa) shall be no less than 15% of NPSHa.

The RCPs are to be driven by direct on-line (DOL) start motors. A variable frequency drive (VFD) system, as well as a motor soft-start system, were considered but ultimately will not be used for the Palisades project [38].

Pumps must be able to be started at full line voltage. Motor design is to accommodate the following when started DOL: (1) high in-rush currents; (2) thermal and mechanical stresses on the motor core and windings; and (3) mechanical stresses on the pump-motor shaft line associated with acceleration of the flywheel to operating speed.
Refer to Section 14.3 for specific RCP motor requirements.

The pump rotating element (shaft assembly) shall consist of the following sub-components: a) Pump drive shaft (motor end) b) Pump shaft (impeller end) c) Pump drive shaft to pump shaft coupling d) Thrust and radial bearings (see Section 14.2.9) e) Pump impeller (see Section 14.2.10)

The pump shaft assembly is to be a split-type design divided into two sections: the pump drive shaft (motor end) and the pump shaft (impeller end) in order to permit servicing of the seal system without removing the motor or disassembling any bearings.
