entries.text: PS-8002-0029, Revision 0.0

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump shaft and drive shaft are to be connected by a metallic splined face, rigid flange coupling to ensure positive reproducibility of shaft alignment. The motor drive shaft is to be coupled to the pump drive shaft by a metallic curved tooth coupling.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump shaft assembly couplings are to be designed to compensate for angular and/or radial misalignments to minimize the thrust transmitted to the motor, and to facilitate pump shaft assembly in the field and pump motor changeouts.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The critical speed is the speed at which the shaft assembly's natural frequency matches the rotational speed, causing resonance. The damped natural frequency of the RCP rotating assembly shall be at least 25% above or 25% below the operating speed to avoid resonance (i.e., a ± 25% separation margin). Modal damping shall be evaluated in accordance with API 610 (12th Edition) to prevent adverse effects.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump shaft and drive shaft materials shall be ASME SA-182 F6NM forgings, or ASME SA-743 CA6NM or ASME SA-487 CA6NM castings, or other Buyer approved materials with equivalent chemical composition, mechanical properties, and corrosion resistance. Pump shafts shall be solid material not hollow.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The Supplier shall perform finite element analyses (FEA) to ensure that the probability of a complete pump shaft shear during all phases of pump operations is less than 10-6 events per reactor year.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Reactor coolant pumps are to utilize shaft seals which are designed to limit the leakage to containment of reactor coolant along the pump shaft. This is to be achieved by using a series of primary and secondary seals. These seals essentially become part of the safety-related reactor coolant system pressure boundary and shall be designed and manufactured in accordance with a 10CFR50 Appendix B QA Program. The primary seals (e.g., metallic oxides, carbides, and graphite, etc.) will limit the leakage of reactor coolant across the interface between rotating and stationary RCS elements. The secondary seals (e.g., elastomer O-rings, U-cups, and channel seals, etc.) will prevent leakage between stationary mechanical elements of the RCS seal or those elements that have only a slight relative motion. The Supplier shall delineate the specific safety-classification of each of the seal components that is required to maintain the RCS pressure boundary safety function.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Pump design shall incorporate hydrodynamic cartridge seal packages. A unit seal cartridge which can be brought into the containment as a complete unit is required to reduce the impact on seal replacement time and plant availability by eliminating the handling the seals within containment in more than one piece.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The minimum design life objective for controlled leakage seals is 50,000 hours of operation at NOP/NOT. Shaft seal life shall be demonstrated either by prior PWR plant experience or by realistic long-term tests of the seals (minimum of 6,000 hours).

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The shaft system shall be designed to allow continued operation of the pump for a period of at least one week, but preferably longer, after failure of one of the several stages in order to permit an orderly plant shutdown, without excessive loss of reactor coolant, in the event of the degradation of a second seal stage. In addition, a backup stage capable of holding against full pressure with the pump idle shall be provided. The required holding time and allowable leakage rate for the backup seal is 168 hours at a maximum leak rate of 1.0 gpm. Seals shall comply with U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) Order EA-12-049 endorsed in JLD-ISG-2012-01 (Feb. 2017).

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Normal operation of the seal package, including anticipated fluctuations in seal boundary conditions such as fluid temperature or pressure, shall not result in inter-seal cavity pressure oscillations in multi-stage seals.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The seal package shall withstand the extended low-pressure operation expected to occur in actual service without damage (e.g., during startup) which would otherwise prevent the seal package from attaining its design life.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Stress and deflection analyses of all seal parts shall be performed to show that no undesired interferences or excessive O-ring extrusion gaps occur as a result of deflections due to mechanical and pressure loadings and temperature changes and that the stresses in the parts are within allowable values. These analyses shall account for worst-case fabrication tolerances and for anticipated operating conditions, including off-normal events and the resultant transient conditions in the seal.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Seals are to be qualified to prevent significant shaft leakage at NOP/NOT during Station Blackout (SBO) conditions, i.e., loss of all electrical power and cooling water (seal injection and CCW) for a period of 72 hours minimum to assure safe plant shutdown. This plant injection design condition is termed "extended loss of AC power" (ELAP).

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: RCPs are to be designed with a backseat provision when the pump is uncoupled from the motor. The backseat design provides a RCS pressure boundary to permit replacement of the seal package and/or motor during plant outages when the refueling cavity is fully filled with water. The weight of the impeller/shaft assembly shall be sufficient to provide pressure boundary control for this maintenance activity. The required static head is estimated to be at least 35 feet of water (approximately 15 psi). It is expected, barring wear, erosion, or imperfect sealing of the backseat seals, that there would be no more than 0-1 gpm continuous leakage in the backseated position. Minimization of backseat leakage is important to prevent both inadvertent draindown of the RCS and to reduce radiation doses to maintenance workers replacing pump seals. The Supplier is to provide the static head value that could lift the assembly off its backseat causing cavity leakage into the maintenance area.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The reactor coolant pump shall be designed such that seal replacement can be achieved without draining down the reactor coolant system and shall minimize the time and effort required in the containment to remove and replace a pump shaft seal. This shall include design features such as improved access for lifting and handling, permanent services at the pumps, special handling equipment and tooling for the seal and coupling parts, and service and instrument connections which can be rapidly connected and disconnected or left in place. It shall be an objective to complete the seal replacement activity in containment within a maximum time limit of two 10-hour shifts.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: Instrumentation shall be provided so that the plant operators can confirm the normal operation of the shaft seal assembly, detect and characterize seal degradation or failure, and monitor operation with degraded or failed stages. Pumps are to be provided with instrumentation sufficient to adequately monitor the sealing system over their anticipated ranges for normal operation (including startups and shutdowns), anticipated operational occurrences, and accident conditions. The provided instrumentation shall be in accordance with Section 14.2.17 of this Specification.

entries.section_title: 14.2.9 Pump Hydraulic Bearings and Lubrication Oil System
entries.text: The pump's rotating element shall be supported horizontally by radial type bearings. The rotating element's dead weight and hydraulic thrust shall be absorbed by thrust type bearings.

entries.section_title: 14.2.9 Pump Hydraulic Bearings and Lubrication Oil System
entries.text: All pump bearings shall provide adequate stiffness to control shaft motion, protect the pump impeller and shaft labyrinths from wear, and avoid contact between the motor stator and rotor. RCP bearings are to provide long life with negligible wear. The bearing loads are to be maintained within component load capabilities even under the severe conditions experienced during seismic events. The bearing/shaft design and loadings are to be established by analysis and testing.

entries.section_title: 14.2.9 Pump Hydraulic Bearings and Lubrication Oil System
entries.text: The pump bearing oil system shall provide the means to lift the pump motor rotor off the thrust bearing to reduce RCP starting current and to allow hand rotation of the rotor to facilitate alignment. An acceptable means of meeting this requirement is a hydraulic oil lift system. An oil lift pump configured for a 480VAC power supply may be mounted externally on the side of the pump housing. The lift system should include a pressure and time permissive (with defeats) prior to starting the RCP.

entries.section_title: 14.2.9 Pump Hydraulic Bearings and Lubrication Oil System
entries.text: The bearing oil system shall be designed in accordance with 10CFR50 Appendix A General Design Criterion (GDC) #3, and USNRC Regulatory Guide 1.189 Revision 5. Overall system design shall not result in posing a fire hazard within the reactor containment structure. The pump lube oil cooler piping system must be designed in accordance with ASME B31.1-2022 and be able to withstand the site safe shutdown earthquake (SSE) loads without oil leakage and without causing an oil fire.

A process for ensuring that equipment will be capable of withstanding the ambient conditions that could exist when the specific function to be performed by the equipment is actually called upon to be performed under accident conditions.
A drawing that contains all of the information in the Design drawings plus second level details required for manufacturing such as sub-assembly details, specific subpart details, etc.

A formal process conducted at the Supplier's facility to verify and validate that a system, equipment, or component complies with contractual requirements, technical specifications, and functional standards before shipment to the customer's site. FAT involves systematic testing of the equipment's functionality, performance, safety features, and documentation under controlled conditions in the factory to identify and resolve any deficiencies prior to delivery.

An identified operation requiring witnessing by the specified party. Operation may not proceed without witnessing of the specified party unless waived by the specified party. For ASME Section III, where an ASME stamp is required, see the definition in the ASME Section III Manual.

A broad term that encompasses safety-related items but also includes other systems and components that contribute to the plant's overall safety and operational reliability. The ITS SSCs prevent, mitigate, or respond to safety hazards but may be classified under the strict "safety-related" category. These items support the plant's safety functions but may also be involved in operational tasks. All safety-related SSCs are important to safety, but not all important-to-safety items are classified as safety-related.

A potential plant unit accident in which a breach in a reactor's pressure boundary causes the coolant water to rush out of the reactor faster than makeup water can be added back in. Without sufficient coolant, the reactor core could heat up and potentially melt the zirconium fuel cladding, causing a major release of radioactivity.

SSCs required to ensure the safe operation of the plant, the prevention of accidents, or the mitigation of their consequences. These systems are primarily focused on supporting the operational efficiency and convenience of the plant but do not directly affect nuclear safety in the event of an accident or emergency. Non-safety-related components are typically designed and installed using commercial-grade parts and equipment.
The period during which an electrical generating unit or its transmission line is out of service. Outages may be forced or scheduled, and full or partial.

The maximum vibratory ground motion for which certain structures, systems, and components must be designed pursuant to Appendix S to 10CFR Part 50 to remain functional. This earthquake is based upon an evaluation of the maximum earthquake potential considering the regional and local geology and seismology and specific characteristics of local subsurface material. These structures, systems, and components are those necessary to ensure the following:

Refers to systems, structures, and components that are directly required to ensure the safe shutdown of the reactor, prevent or mitigate accidents, and maintain containment of radioactive materials. They are relied upon to remain functional during and following design-basis events. Their functionality ensures that key regulatory criteria, such as levels of radioactivity released, are met.

A coating system used in areas inside the reactor containment structure where coating failure could adversely affect the operation of post-accident fluid systems and thereby impair safe reactor shutdown. The coating is designed to withstand design basis incidents within the reactor containment structure without flaking or degrading.

Part of factory acceptance testing for a pump/motor assembly. The testing is designed to simulate the real-world operating conditions of the system over an extended period, ensuring that both the pump and motor can reliably perform as expected under normal and varying loads. This test evaluates the durability, performance, and efficiency of the assembly, focusing on its long-term operational reliability.

One potential acceptable method to meet these requirements is the use of double (i.e., two separate) flange gaskets with a means to monitor the space between the two gaskets.

The leakage detection method shall have enough sensitivity such that leakage can be detected before the represents a major operational problem; however, it shall not result in false leakage indications. The detection method shall allow for continuous monitoring and remote indication and alarming.

entries.section_title: Pump Design Provisions Due to Absence of RCS Vacuum Fill
entries.text: The Holtec SMR-300 plant will not be provided with provisions to vacuum fill the reactor coolant system after refueling outages. Use of a vacuum system for refilling the RCS after the system is drained for maintenance or refueling via the removal of air and non-condensable gases would, if utilized, reduce the time required for RCS fill and potentially reduce the wear and tear on the reactor coolant pumps. The RCPs shall be designed with suitable provisions, as deemed necessary by the Supplier, to prevent potential pump hydraulic damage over the plant lifetime as the result of pump startup with the RCS piping less than 100% full of coolant.

In the Holtec SMR-300 RCS, the two RCPs will be operated in parallel at 100% power, with one pump in each cold leg. The Supplier is required to consider and address problems associated with potential parallel pump operational configurations for both hot and cold coolant conditions including, but not limited to the following:
Only one of the two pumps running with reverse flow through the idle pump.
Flow imbalance between running pumps.
NPSH discharge flows significantly lower than the best efficiency point (BEP).

Motor current starting draw for the various parallel pump operational configurations must also be considered for both hot and cold conditions. Both pumps are expected to be operated at cold conditions during Mode 5 (Cold Shutdown) with a RCS average temperature of approximately 200 °F (or less) for 12 to 36 hours for chemical addition purposes (i.e., crude burst).
The preliminary system resistance curve for cold startup condition is shown in the figure below and is subject to change.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: PS-8002-0029, Revision 0.0

To ensure stable pumping over the entire range of operation, the characteristics of each pump should be such that an increase in head always produces a decrease in flow, i.e., rising head-capacity characteristic. The head-flow characteristic curves for pumps used in parallel operation should constantly rise toward shutoff, and these curves should also be similar enough to assure that the pumps will operate at the same point and divide the load evenly. The two RCS piping cold legs (refer to Appendix A) will essentially consist of the exact same configuration and it is thus required that the two pumps operate uniformly and in concert. It is expected that two pumps operating in parallel will operate at the same head but at double the flow rate of an individual pump.

The pump casing design corrosion allowance shall be 0.032" (minimum) except if ASME Section III requires a higher value otherwise. The pump casings and impellers will process water with the chemistry composition as indicated in Appendix D. It must be assured that the pump can operate or sit stagnant in high boric acid concentrations (up to 2,600 ppm) with no adverse long-term effects, e.g., pitting corrosion or any other loss of pressure boundary material.

To reduce the buildup of corrosion products and improve the future ability to decontaminate the interior of the casings, the casings' interior stainless steel shall be electro-polished and passivated. The intent is to significantly reduce the radiation dose to ALARA levels for personnel during pump and motor maintenance activities.

It is noted that the initial average surface roughness (Ra) of forged or cast stainless steel can vary based on the manufacturing process, machining, and finishing. The electropolishing process typically results in a roughness reduction of up to 50%. For example, assuming an initial Ra of 80 microinches, after electropolishing the improved Ra would be approximately 40 microinches. The requested criterion for the final polishing would be an approximate 50% reduction from the starting average roughness value. The Code required minimum wall thickness for the casings and the specified cladding thickness shall be maintained after electropolishing.

The Buyer requires the pump assembly support design to consist of feet integrally attached to the casing. The support system feet must be sufficient to carry the entire weight of the pump and motor and ultimately must be designed to allow for thermal expansion and to withstand the expected operating and SSE loads. The Supplier shall incorporate adequate additional support points into the pump and motor as needed. These support locations must be identified on the design drawings. Additional information on pump and motor supports is contained in Section 14.2.18 of this Specification.

The pump impeller shall be both statically and dynamically balanced for maximum efficiency and smooth operation without detrimental vibrations over the entire range of anticipated operations, including extended times at low speeds and during speed increases of up to 125% of rated speed.
The rotating element shall be mechanically balanced to preclude vibration.

The pump assembly shall be hydraulically balanced by design and shall include use of flow splitters/straighteners if necessary, also to preclude vibration. The Supplier shall contact the Buyer's Technical Contact to confirm the final layout and orientation of the pump suction piping. entries.text: The pump shaft is to be divided into two sections joined by a rigid coupling. This split design is required to permit servicing of the seal system without removing the motor or disassembling the combination journal and thrust bearing. The rigid coupling must be designed to compensate for angular and/or radial misalignments.

entries.section_title: Purchase Specification for SMR-300 Reactor Coolant Pumps
entries.text: The pump and seal cartridge shall be designed to allow the pump to be self-venting during fill without use of special venting connections to the pump. The staging or leak-off flow path inside the pump and seal cartridge shall avoid "high spots" which can trap air during venting. Similarly, the pump design shall include drain line provisions where necessary to allow emptying water from the pump bowl to facilitate maintenance.

Commercial grade items may be upgraded to safety-related quality standards under a formal dedication process.

Those important design, material, and performance characteristics of a commercial grade item that, once verified, will provide reasonable assurance that the item will perform its intended safety function.
The critical speed of a vertical centrifugal pump shaft is the speed at which the shaft's natural frequency matches the rotational speed, causing resonance.
Any deviation from a regulatory requirement, design basis, or manufacturing process that could result in a substantial safety hazard.
A postulated accident that a nuclear facility must be designed and built to withstand without loss to the systems, structures, and components necessary to ensure public health and safety.

A formal process conducted at the Supplier's facility to verify and validate that a system, equipment, or component complies with contractual requirements, technical specifications, and functional standards before shipment to the customer's site. An identified operation requiring witnessing by the specified party. Operation may not proceed without witnessing of the specified party unless waived by the specified party. For ASME Section III, where an ASME stamp is required, see the definition in the ASME Section III Manual.

A broad term that encompasses safety-related items but also includes other systems and components that contribute to the plant's overall safety and operational reliability. These items support the plant's safety functions but may also be involved in operational tasks. All safety-related SSCs are important to safety, but not all important-to-safety items are classified as safety-related.

The following are the minimum requirements for the cleaning, packaging, and shipment of the competed pump assemblies. The intent of the following requirements is to ensure protection against corrosion, contamination, physical damage, or any effect which would lower the quality or cause the pump assemblies to deteriorate during the entire time the items are being shipped, handled, and stored.
Cleaning and cleanliness control of the completed pump assemblies shall be in accordance with Subpart 2.1 of ASME NQA-1 for Class B.

Items, just before packaging, shall have been inspected for cleanliness. Dirt, oil residue, metal chips or other forms of contamination shall have been removed by approved cleaning methods. Any entrapped water shall have been removed.

The pump assemblies shall be packaged assuming long-term site storage.
All motor leads and other motor entrances to internal wiring shall be effectively protected or sealed, to prevent entrance of moisture, dust, and dirt.
All openings into items shall be capped, plugged, and sealed. Weld end preparations shall be protected from corrosion and physical damage.

entries.text: Pump parts not in contact with the reactor coolant must be of a corrosion-resistant material or otherwise coated per Section 14.10 of this Specification. All materials in contact with RCS, CVC, and CCW fluids must be compatible with all other supplied materials to not cause cathodic corrosion concerns. RCS piping chemical decontamination will be required periodically over the plant life to minimize personnel radiation exposures. All reactor coolant pump parts wetted by primary coolant shall be compatible with standard PWR chemical decontamination solutions. It is anticipated that standard PWR chemical decontamination solutions will be periodically utilized over the plant's life. Decontamination processes that may be used include but are not limited to: CANDEREM (citric acid and EDTA), CITROX (citric acid and oxalic acid), NITROX / NITROX-E (nitric acid, oxalic acid and potassium permanganate). Frequency of decontamination will depend on plant needs to keep the primary piping and RCP casing dose rates as low as reasonably achievable (ALARA). Decontamination will be performed when needed during plant outages to the specific process and quantities of the chemicals used will depend on the isotopes to be removed and the radiation dose reduction required. In the event compatibility with the anticipated chemical decontamination solutions cannot be achieved, incompatible parts shall be designed to either be removed from the pump or otherwise have provisions allowing isolation from the decontamination solution. Such parts shall be clearly delineated on the Supplier's design drawings. The allowable heating and cooling rate of parts exposed to the high temperature reactor coolant shall be at least 100 °F/hr.

Bolted joints and threaded fasteners should be used only where a clear need for them has been established. The use of a bolted joint should include consideration of not only the first cost but the subsequent maintenance effort, the risk of service problems, and the risk of collecting radioactive material which such joints can introduce. Where a bolted joint must be used to satisfy functional requirements, its adequacy should preferentially be achieved by a simple, rugged design which does not depend on high strength or unusual materials, precision parts, or specialized assembly and inspection methods.

Threaded fasteners should be locked under the following conditions: (1) where the threaded fasteners are subjected to alternating loads which are a significant fraction of their minimum pre-load and especially where the fastener's pre-load could be released by small deformations of the fastener or joint parts; or (2) where the threaded fastener cannot be pre-loaded significantly even though the expected loads are small.

A locking device shall: (1) not have any parts which vibrate excessively; (2) require a minimum of technician skill to disassemble and reassemble; and (3) allow for easy inspection and verification of proper installation without disassembly.

Fasteners shall be locked by a method which retains the broken fastener parts. Where failure of the load carrying portion of a single threaded fastener will result in a loose part which has a high probability of causing damage to other components which would result in serious personal injury or require extensive down time or high cost to repair, the locking means shall provide for the retention of the broken fastener parts as well as preventing rotation.

Bolted joints must be easily inspectable, located on the exterior of the pump assembly, and not be covered or obscured by other components (where possible) to allow for the required ASME B&PV Code Section XI Inservice Inspection (ISI) non-destructive examination (NDE) purposes.

entries.text: Any special tools necessary for the maintenance, disassembly, and reassembly of the RCP pump assemblies shall be furnished by the Supplier in the quantities listed on the Purchase Order. These tools may include, but are not limited to, the following:

entries.text: PS-8002-0029, Revision 0.0

Generally, the RCP assemblies shall be constructed with only materials which have been proven by experience to be suitable for light water reactor (LWR) service. Materials which have seen little or no LWR service are not entirely prohibited, but proven materials are preferred. A written justification for the use of unproven materials, or for the use of materials not contained in ASME Section II, shall be provided. The justification shall discuss why the listed or unproven material is being selected and the basis on which the Supplier considers it to be acceptable. This justification should address peak stresses and strains, local water chemistry, expected radiation environment, and temperature at the point of specific application.

In general, all pump parts except the bearings and seal faces that are in contact with the reactor coolant and injection water should be of austenitic or other stainless steel, Inconel, or an equivalent corrosion resistant material. Carbon and alloy steels with weld-deposited austenitic stainless steel or non-air-hardening Inconel cladding are acceptable for pressure boundary parts. The carbon content measured at the surface of the cladding must not exceed 0.10%.

Pump parts not in contact with the reactor coolant must be of a corrosion-resistant material or otherwise coated per Section 14.10 of this Specification. All materials in contact with RCS, CVC, and CCW fluids must be compatible with all other supplied materials to not cause cathodic corrosion concerns.

RCS piping chemical decontamination will be required periodically over the plant life to minimize personnel radiation exposures. All reactor coolant pump parts wetted by primary coolant shall be compatible with standard PWR chemical decontamination solutions.

It is anticipated that standard PWR chemical decontamination solutions will be periodically utilized over the plant's life. Decontamination processes that may be used include but are not limited to: CANDEREM (citric acid and EDTA), CITROX (citric acid and oxalic acid), NITROX / NITROX-E (nitric acid, oxalic acid and potassium permanganate). Frequency of decontamination will depend on plant needs to keep the primary piping and RCP casing dose rates as low as reasonably achievable (ALARA). Decontamination will be performed when needed during plant outages to the specific process and quantities of the chemicals used will depend on the isotopes to be removed and the radiation dose reduction required.

In the event compatibility with the anticipated chemical decontamination solutions cannot be achieved, incompatible parts shall be designed to either be removed from the pump or otherwise have provisions allowing isolation from the decontamination solution. Such parts shall be clearly delineated on the Supplier's design drawings.
The allowable heating and cooling rate of parts exposed to the high temperature reactor coolant shall be at least 100 °F/hr.

entries.text: The analysis of flywheel capture is to be predicated on energy calculations, presented as a fraction of the energy necessary to totally breach the motor housing. Each flywheel requires testing at an overspeed condition under both normal RCS cold and hot conditions to verify the flywheel design and construction.

Additionally, if an internal flywheel is used in the RCP, the design and construction of the flywheel shall minimize areas of high stress concentration, provide suitable material toughness, and implement all the fabrication and examination procedures necessary to achieve a high level of integrity throughout the plant's operating life.

Access to the flywheel for maintenance will require pump and/or motor removal and disassembly, which would increase personnel radiation exposure and potentially impact plant availability. The flywheel should therefore be designed such that planned maintenance and inspection activities are not required beyond those already planned for the pump assembly itself. The Supplier shall show that the flywheel design is such that it does not add to the burden of pump maintenance and does not require periodic in-service inspection, other than that which may be regulatory required.

For a motor-mounted flywheel, overspeed testing with the motor uncoupled from the pump is acceptable. Testing of the flywheel at hot and cold RCS conditions would only be required for a flywheel located inside the pump casing which is exposed to RCS temperature conditions.

The design of the pump shall be such as to preclude the instantaneous stopping of any rotating component of the pump or motor. Due to the potential significant effect on the reactor core and RCS pressure due to RCP motor seizure (i.e., locked rotor) of one or both pumps while the plant is at power, the Supplier shall provide the failure mechanisms and the probability of the instantaneous complete stopping of any pump assembly rotating element with the plant at full power, i.e., RCPs at nominal full speed and RCS conditions at NOP/NOT. An instantaneous stop of the impeller is considered a conservative assumption that bounds any slower stop or coast down. This information will allow Holtec to perform a transient analysis to determine the effect of a locked rotor on the RCS pressure and RCS pressure which will be necessary to demonstrate that acceptable reactor core and boundary radiological consequence limits are not exceeded due to departure from nucleate boiling (DNB).
The stresses in the pump casing and motor housing are to be analyzed using the ASME B&PV Code, Section III, Service Level D limits for this condition.

The SMR-300 normal operating conditions are similar to existing PWRs (2,250 psia NOP, 546 °F NOT). The initiating events for the SMR-300 are also similar to existing PWRs. Therefore, it is expected that the SMR-300 RCPs will experience similar conditions as existing PWRs.

entries.section_title: The pump shaft is to be divided into two sections joined by a rigid coupling
entries.text: The pump shaft is to be divided into two sections joined by a rigid coupling. This split design is required to permit servicing of the seal system without removing the motor or disassembling the combination journal and thrust bearing.

entries.section_title: The rigid coupling must be designed to compensate for angular and/or radial misalignments
entries.text: The rigid coupling must be designed to compensate for angular and/or radial misalignments.

[1] The materials of all pump hydraulic pressure-retaining parts in direct contact with the reactor coolant must conform with the requirements set forth in Section III of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, 2021 Edition. ASME Section III requires the use of the materials listed in ASME Section II. Other materials of the pump must conform to the requirements of the specifications for materials listed in this Code. The requirements of USNRC Regulatory Guide (RG) 1.84, "Design, Fabrication, and Materials Code Case Acceptability; ASME Section III" shall also apply.

[2] If other than ASME Section III/II listed materials are to be used for primary pressure-retaining parts (e.g., ISO, EN, RCC-M, etc.), a formal ASME code reconciliation as described in Subsection NCA is required to demonstrate equivalency for each substitution. All such analyses shall be included in the pump assembly's documentation package.

[3] The ASME Section III/II material requirements and code reconciliation requirements in [2] above do not apply to items that are not associated with the pressure-retaining function of the pump, such as shafts, trim, bearings, bushings, wear plates, seals, packing, and gaskets.
[4] Piping materials for the CVC, CCW and motor lube oil cooling piping shall comply with ASME B31.1-2022 requirements.
